name: CI
display_title: Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

head_commit.message:
Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

`HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only lets a temporary reuse the buffer of an operand value if the user consumes the defining instruction of that value directly. A user that reads the value only through other positions (e.g. two `get-tuple-element`s of a tuple, or a bitcast) never reuses the buffer, even if every read is elementwise.

Since `CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser` checks every use of the value by the user, this restriction is no longer needed for correctness. So this change removes it for chunk-assigning heap algorithms, while keeping stats-only runs (`NoFragmentationStatsHeap` in `MinimumMemoryForModule`) restricted to direct operands so schedule scoring in `DefaultMemoryScheduler` does not change.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1020624697

display_title: [TF/XLA] Finalize Bazel 8 Bzlmod cleanup and mark XLA extensions reproducible.

head_commit.message:
[TF/XLA] Finalize Bazel 8 Bzlmod cleanup and mark XLA extensions reproducible.

Clean up remaining Bazel 8 / Bzlmod migration items across TensorFlow and XLA:
* Pin `envoy_api` to `0.0.0-20260130-84e8436` in TensorFlow's `MODULE.bazel`
  (matching XLA) so `bazel mod show_repo --all_repos` resolves cleanly.
* Fix Windows `ERROR_FILENAME_EXCED_RANGE` ("The filename or extension is too
  long") when loading `.pyd` extensions in the 251-259 char path range under
  Bzlmod (`rules_python`'s `_WindowsExtensionPathFinder` only added `\\?\` at
  `>= 260` chars, missing Win32 `LoadLibraryExW` `.manifest` probing) via
  `//third_party/py:rules_python_windows_long_path.patch`.
* Remove obsolete `--features=-external_include_paths` and
  `--host_features=-external_include_paths` from `.bazelrc` and XLA's
  `tensorflow.bazelrc` (now that `rules_cc` is `0.2.25 >= 0.2.22`), propagate
  `CompilationContext.external_includes` through `system_includes` in
  `xla/tsl/transitive_dependencies.bzl` (`_transitive_parameters_library_impl`,
  used by `custom_op_cc_header_only_library` such as
  `//tensorflow/core:framework_headers_lib`), and remove the duplicate
  `common:windows --features=compiler_param_file`.
* Mark deterministic XLA module extensions reproducible via
  `mctx.extension_metadata(reproducible = True)` (all 12 remaining extensions
  under `third_party/` and `build_tools/pjrt_wheels/`).
* Replace deprecated `$(location ...)` with `$(execpath ...)` in
  `tensorflow/tools/pip_package/BUILD`, bump `BAZEL_VERSION` to `8.8.2` in
  `tensorflow/tools/ci_build/install/install_bazel_from_source.sh`, and
  document the Bazel 8.8.2 / Bzlmod and C++/CUDA dependency upgrades in
  `RELEASE.md`.

name: CI
display_title: Clear incompatible tiled sharding on TopK custom calls in xla::TopkRewriter.

head_commit.message:
Clear incompatible tiled sharding on TopK custom calls in xla::TopkRewriter.

`CreateTopKCustomCall` creates the 2D `TopK` custom call, its
`get-tuple-element` outputs, and its input/output `reshape` and `transpose`
instructions via `sort->AddInstruction(...)`, which calls
`SetupDerivedInstruction` and copies `sort`'s sharding whenever the tuple tree
structure matches (`ShapeUtil::CompatibleKind`). When `sort` has rank > 2 (so
its input is reshaped to 2D before `TopK` and reshaped back afterward) or is 2D
with `sort_dim == 0` (so its input is transposed before `TopK` and transposed
back afterward), a tiled sharding on `sort` has the wrong rank or transposed
tile dimensions for the 2D `TopK` custom call, its `get-tuple-element`
instructions, and (for 1-operand sorts) the input/output `reshape` and
`transpose` instructions. Clear tiled sharding on `sort` before creating those
instructions while preserving non-tiled shardings (such as `{manual}` or
`{replicated}`) and 1D/2D `sort_dim == 1` tiled shardings.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019731683

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:CPU] Add AVX-512 kernels for 4-bit PackIntN and UnpackIntN.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Add AVX-512 kernels for 4-bit PackIntN and UnpackIntN.

The generic `LoadInterleaved2` and `StoreInterleaved2` loops in `xla/packing.cc` expand to multi-step cross-lane byte shuffles and fall back to scalar loops for tails shorter than 128 elements, bottlenecking 4-bit tensor packing and unpacking on AVX-512 CPUs.

Add AVX-512 (`HWY_AVX3` and newer) paths to `Pack4Impl` and `Unpack4Impl`:

* `Pack4Impl` masks inputs to 4 bits, combines adjacent byte pairs via `SatWidenMulPairwiseAdd` (`vpmaddubsw` with `(1, 16)` multipliers), and narrows two vectors with `OrderedDemote2To` (`vpackuswb` + `vpermq`), with a single masked `vpmovwb` store path for inputs up to 64 elements. On `HWY_AVX3_DL` and `HWY_AVX3_SPR`, an empty inline-assembly barrier on the multiplier prevents LLVM from fusing `vpackuswb` + `vpermq` into `vpermt2b` (3 uops on Intel instead of 2, which slowed down 1024–10000 element calls by 8–14%), while `HWY_AVX3_ZEN4` retains the fused instruction.
* `Unpack4Impl` zero-extends 32 packed bytes to 16-bit lanes and computes `(wide | (wide << 4)) & 0x0F0F`.
* Both kernels handle sub-vector tails with AVX-512BW masked loads and stores and use a manual 4x unrolled loop followed by a `HWY_UNROLL(1)` 1x loop to avoid LLVM's runtime-unroll trip-count setup on small inputs (except `Unpack4Impl` on `HWY_AVX3`, where LLVM's default loop is 4.7% faster at 10000 elements).

Across 37 to 1048576 elements, this speeds up `PackIntN<4>` by 1.31× geomean on Sapphire Rapids / Emerald Rapids / Granite Rapids (1.30× on Emerald Rapids), 1.24× on Zen 4/5, and 1.40× on Skylake-SP / Cascade Lake, and speeds up `UnpackIntN<4>` by 1.25×, 1.18×, and 1.17× geomean respectively.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1020557305

name: CI
display_title: Fix TF loop event grouping with ThreadpoolListener::Region.

head_commit.message:
Fix TF loop event grouping with ThreadpoolListener::Region.

When a TensorFlow `while_loop` runs in the executor, `NextIteration` in iteration `k` can activate `Merge` for iteration `k + 1` inline on the same worker thread inside a single `ThreadpoolListener::Region` closure (or schedule tasks for iteration `k + 1` before `iteration_scope` updates). Enabling consumer context stats on `ThreadpoolListener::Region` previously caused iteration `k`'s group propagation to overwrite subsequent loop iterations into a single step group, and left duplicate consumer stats on paired `ThreadpoolListener::StartRegion` markers.

- Track active regions with a stack in `ThreadpoolLineMutator::MutateEventsInLine` (supporting zero-timestamp starts, nested inline closures, and `uint64_t` region IDs), copy `ContextType::kThreadpoolEvent` consumer stats onto `ThreadpoolListener::Region`, and strip consumer stats from paired `StartRegion` markers so `AddFlowsToXplane` emits a single `kFlowIn` endpoint per region.
- Pre-assign `group_id` to all entry `ExecutorState::Process` events of each TensorFlow loop iteration in `EventForest::ProcessTensorFlowLoop`, and update `EventNode::PropagateGroupId` so BFS expands nodes matching `group_id` while stopping at nodes pre-assigned to other groups.
- Skip intra-thread parent edges onto `ProcessBatch` and `OrbaxServing::ProcessBatch` in `EventForest::ConnectIntraThread` so chained batch scheduler closures do not merge distinct batches across `ThreadpoolListener::Region`.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:CPU] Lower log and log1p to YNNPACK SIMD bitcode kernels.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Lower log and log1p to YNNPACK SIMD bitcode kernels.

### Status quo

In the XLA:CPU MLIR fusion pipeline, `f32` `log` uses a handwritten LLVM IR polynomial (`GenerateVF32Log`, 1.19 ULP max error), `f64` `log` falls back to scalar `libm` `log` calls (0.5 ULP, unvectorized), and `log1p` lowers to an algebraic composition around `log` (up to ~3.0 ULP in `f32`).

### Why

Compiling YNNPACK's `log` and `log1p` SIMD kernels (`f32` and `f64`, up to 512-bit vectors) to LLVM bitcode and inlining them during codegen vectorizes `f64` `log` and `log1p`, speeds up `f32` `log` and `log1p` across x86 and ARM64, improves `f32` accuracy (`log` 1.19 -> 1.02 ULP, `log1p` 3.0 -> 1.65 ULP), and deletes XLA:CPU's handwritten `GenerateVF32Log` C++ IR builder.

End-to-end `elementwise_benchmark_test` (`N = 128, 1024, 8192` geomean cycles/op vs baseline):
- `f32` (`BM_LogF32`, `BM_Log1pF32`): `-19.1%` on x86 AVX2+FMA3, `-28.8%` on x86 AVX-512, `-36.6%` on ARM64 NEON.
- `f64` (`BM_LogF64`, `BM_Log1pF64`): `1.7x-4.4x` faster across AVX2, AVX-512, and ARM64 NEON.

### Design choices

- Expose YNNPACK `log` and `log1p` wrappers for `f32` and `f64` vector widths up to 512 bits in `xla/codegen/intrinsic/cpp/ynnpack_unary.{h,cc}`, compile a single `ynnpack_unary_ll` bitcode library, inline from it during codegen, and stop splitting `v16f32` `log` on AVX-512.
- Keep upcasting `f16` and `bf16` to `f32`, since YNNPACK has no native full-precision 16-bit `log`/`log1p` kernels on x86.
- Preserve `log1p(-0.0) = -0.0` via `copysign`, and keep the existing `libm` and algebraic `Log1p` lowerings on GPU and when CppGen bitcode is unavailable.

### Compromises

Maximum error bounds in ULPs (from JAX's numerics test suite and `docs/accuracy.md`):

| Op | CPU (before) | CPU (this CL) | NVIDIA GPU | TPU (v6e / 7x) |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| `log` (`f32`) | 1.5 | 1.5 | 1.0 | 2.5 |
| `log` (`f64`) | 0.5 | 1.5 | 1.5 | N/A |
| `log1p` (`f32`) | 3.0 | 2.0 | 1.0 | 3.0 |
| `log1p` (`f64`) | 2.0 | 2.0 | 1.5 | N/A |
| `log10` (`f32`) | 3.0 | 2.5 | 2.5 | 3.0 |
| `logit` (`f32`) | 3.0 | 2.0 | 3.0 | 4.0 / 4.5 |
| `acosh` (`f32`) | 4.5 | 3.5 | 2.5 | 4.5 / 5.0 |
| `asinh` (`f32`) | 3.5 | 2.0 | 2.0 | 3.5 |
| `atanh` (`f32`) | 3.0 | 2.0 | 3.5 | 3.5 |

`f64` `log` trades scalar `libm`'s 0.5 ULP correct rounding for SIMD vectorization, matching GPU's 1.5 ULP bound (measured 1.23 ULP).

The `c128` `Log` exhaustive test gets a 1 ULP relative bound on CPU for inputs with tiny imaginary parts. CPU already flushes those imaginary parts to zero, which fails the distance check, so the real part `log|z|` was effectively held to exact `libm` results.

### Alternatives

- Tested a pure degree-8 Estrin polynomial (`Q = 1`) for `f32` `log` in YNNPACK, which avoided `fdiv` latency in isolation on wide AVX-512 vectors, but ran slower in XLA's unrolled elementwise loops across AVX2, AVX-512, and ARM64 NEON than the `[3/2]` rational kernel.
- Reaching `<= 1.0` ULP for both `log` and `log1p` requires split `ln(2)` plus double-word addition for `1 + x`, which added 18-68% per-vector overhead in microbenchmarks for accuracy tighter than GPU (`f64`) and TPU (`f32`).

### Updating tests

CPU `log` and `log1p` results move by about 1 ULP on many inputs, and by more in code that amplifies small differences (iterative solves, log-dets, KL divergences, derivatives). Tests that check exact equality, use tolerances below 1 ULP, or compare against goldens captured from the old output may fail. Please update them to allow a few ULP, or set goldens to exact reference values, rather than pinning bit-exact results.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA][HLO Value Tracking] Propagate OriginalValue in TupleUtil.

head_commit.message:
[XLA][HLO Value Tracking] Propagate OriginalValue in TupleUtil.

`TupleUtil::ExtractPrefix`, `AppendSuffix`, `Duplicate`, `ReplaceTupleWith`, and `AddGetTupleElements` create `tuple`, `get-tuple-element`, and `bitcast` instructions without an `OriginalValue`, so every caller that wants to preserve HLO value tracking has to patch the original values up by hand after each call. Callers that don't (e.g. for the intermediate instructions `ReplaceTupleWith` creates for nested tuples) silently lose value tracking.

Since every element these helpers create holds the same value as the element it is taken from, derive the `OriginalValue`s of the created instructions from those of their inputs. An input's `OriginalValue` is only used if it matches the input's shape; inputs whose shape was changed in place without updating their `OriginalValue` leave the derived instructions without one, as before, instead of risking a crash or a misattributed value. Callers that widen shapes in place are responsible for keeping the `OriginalValue` in sync, which the new `AppendEmptyElementsToOriginalValue` helper does for the common case of appending tuple elements.

Update the callers accordingly:

* `WhileUtil::MakeInstructionsLiveIn` no longer copies `OriginalValue`s onto the results of `AppendSuffix` and `ExtractPrefix`.
* `HloControlFlowFlattening` and `WhileLoopIterationCap` keep the `OriginalValue`s of the instructions they widen in place in sync before building tuples from them, which also replaces the `AppendToWhileLoopOriginalValue` call in `WhileLoopIterationCap`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1020427267

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Size F32 RAFT select_k scratch buffers dynamically.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Size F32 RAFT select_k scratch buffers dynamically.

`TopkSpecializer` previously allocated a hardcoded 32 MiB scratch buffer for every RAFT `__gpu$TopK` custom call, over-allocating on small TopK shapes (for example, 32 MiB instead of 4.5 KiB for `f32[8]`) while risking `FixedBufferDeviceMemoryResource` exhaustion on large batch or vocabulary shapes.

Extract `choose_select_k_algorithm_float` into host-only `xla/backends/gpu/runtime/raft_select_k_utils` (shared with `select_k_exec_raft_float.cc`) alongside `EstimateRaftSelectKScratchBytesFloat` and `GetRaftSelectKMaxSmCount`. The estimator bounds WarpSort and two-phase Radix workspace allocations across CUDA thread-block occupancy outcomes and full-die architecture SM ceilings (covering cross-SKU and MIG-to-full-GPU execution), and adds a `max(4 KiB, ~6.25%)` 256-byte-aligned safety margin.

Update `TopkSpecializer` to take `se::DeviceDescription` directly and size `F32` `__gpu$TopK` scratch buffers via `EstimateRaftSelectKScratchBytesFloat` (`BF16` and `U64` remain on the 32 MiB fallback for follow-up changes). Use `RaftScratchPhaseMode::kSumAcrossPhases` during the 14-day GPU AOT forward-compatibility window, and regenerate `v2` GPU AOT compatibility goldens (`f32[8]` `k=1` preallocated scratch drops from 32.00 MiB to 4.5 KiB).

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1020434628

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Add non pageable temporary buffer region option to BufferAssigner

Some temporary buffers are addressed by an external agent at a fixed offset and
cannot be split into or moved across pages under multi page buffer assignment.
Add `BufferAssigner::Options::must_be_non_pageable` and
`BufferAllocation::is_non_pageable()` (persisted in `BufferAllocationProto`) so
callers can pack those buffers in a dedicated unpaged temporary allocation
across disjoint lifetimes. Covered by `buffer_assignment_test`.

name: CI
display_title: [TF] Remove `rules_python_local_wheel.patch` in favor of `local_wheel_repo`.

head_commit.message:
[TF] Remove `rules_python_local_wheel.patch` in favor of `local_wheel_repo`.

Replace the `rules_python_local_wheel.patch` `single_version_override` and the
custom `pip.parse(local_wheels = ...)` attribute with a self-contained Starlark
repository rule (`local_wheel_repo` / `@local_tf_wheel`). Under Bzlmod,
`single_version_override` is ignored for non-root modules, so downstream
projects depending on TensorFlow via `MODULE.bazel` saw unpatched `rules_python`
and failed with `unknown attribute local_wheels provided`.

* Delete `third_party/py/rules_python_local_wheel.patch` and remove it along
  with `pip.parse(local_wheels = ...)` from `MODULE.bazel`.
* Add `third_party/extensions/local_wheel.bzl` (`local_wheel_repo`), a lazy,
  non-reproducible repository rule exposing `dist/<WHEEL_NAME>-*.whl` as
  `@local_tf_wheel//:whl` (watches `dist/` for incremental rebuilds, supports
  hyphen/underscore `WHEEL_NAME` variants, and safely produces an empty
  `filegroup` when `dist/` is absent).
* Update `tf_wheel_dep()` in `tensorflow/tools/pip_package/utils/tf_wheel.bzl`
  to return `@local_tf_wheel//:whl` under Bzlmod while keeping
  `@pypi//<WHEEL_NAME>:whl` under `--config=workspace`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1020417079

name: CI
display_title: Fix GPU integer `tf.math.pow` mismatch with CPU/NumPy for exponents >= 64.

head_commit.message:
Fix GPU integer `tf.math.pow` mismatch with CPU/NumPy for exponents >= 64.

Previously, the MLIR-generated GPU `Pow` kernel lowered `stablehlo.power` to a Linalg/SCF exponentiation-by-squaring loop with a hardcoded upper bound of 6 iterations, which only inspected the lowest 6 bits of the exponent (`y % 64`) and discarded bits at positions >= 6. In addition, MHLO's `PowOp` scalar lowering used a fixed 6-iteration loop bound and a special-case even-base `select` that forced even bases with exponents >= 64 to 0. As a result, odd bases with exponents >= 64 (such as `(-47)**66`) and even bases with exponents >= 64 produced inconsistent results compared to CPU and NumPy fixed-width two's-complement wrap-around semantics.

Update the integer `Pow` lowering across `kernel_gen` and MHLO:
- In `LegalizeTensorReshapePass`, add a post-lowering rewrite (`FixIntegerPowLoopUpperBound`) that updates the `scf.for` loop upper bound emitted by `StablehloLegalizeToLinalgPass` from 6 to the integer element bit-width.
- In MHLO (`map_mhlo_to_scalar_op.h`), iterate up to the integer element bit-width and remove the special-case even-base select so both odd and even bases wrap consistently across all bit-widths.

Fixes #118202

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Size F32 RAFT select_k scratch buffers dynamically.

`TopkSpecializer` previously allocated a hardcoded 32 MiB scratch buffer for every RAFT `__gpu$TopK` custom call, over-allocating on small TopK shapes (for example, 32 MiB instead of 4.5 KiB for `f32[8]`) while risking `FixedBufferDeviceMemoryResource` exhaustion on large batch or vocabulary shapes.

Extract `choose_select_k_algorithm_float` into host-only `xla/backends/gpu/runtime/raft_select_k_utils` (shared with `select_k_exec_raft_float.cc`) alongside `EstimateRaftSelectKScratchBytesFloat` and `GetRaftSelectKMaxSmCount`. The estimator bounds WarpSort and two-phase Radix workspace allocations across CUDA thread-block occupancy outcomes and full-die architecture SM ceilings (covering cross-SKU and MIG-to-full-GPU execution), and adds a `max(4 KiB, ~6.25%)` 256-byte-aligned safety margin.

Update `TopkSpecializer` to take `se::DeviceDescription` directly and size `F32` `__gpu$TopK` scratch buffers via `EstimateRaftSelectKScratchBytesFloat` (`BF16` and `U64` remain on the 32 MiB fallback for follow-up changes). Use `RaftScratchPhaseMode::kSumAcrossPhases` during the 14-day GPU AOT forward-compatibility window, and regenerate `v2` GPU AOT compatibility goldens (`f32[8]` `k=1` preallocated scratch drops from 32.00 MiB to 4.5 KiB).

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:CPU] Lower log and log1p to YNNPACK SIMD bitcode kernels.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Lower log and log1p to YNNPACK SIMD bitcode kernels.

### Status quo

In the XLA:CPU MLIR fusion pipeline, `f32` `log` uses a handwritten LLVM IR polynomial (`GenerateVF32Log`, 1.19 ULP max error), `f64` `log` falls back to scalar `libm` `log` calls (0.5 ULP, unvectorized), and `log1p` lowers to an algebraic composition around `log` (up to ~3.0 ULP in `f32`).

### Why

Compiling YNNPACK's `log` and `log1p` SIMD kernels (`f32` and `f64`, up to 512-bit vectors) to LLVM bitcode and inlining them during codegen vectorizes `f64` `log` and `log1p`, speeds up `f32` `log` and `log1p` across x86 and ARM64, improves `f32` accuracy (`log` 1.19 -> 1.02 ULP, `log1p` 3.0 -> 1.65 ULP), and deletes XLA:CPU's handwritten `GenerateVF32Log` C++ IR builder.

End-to-end `elementwise_benchmark_test` (`N = 128, 1024, 8192` geomean cycles/op vs baseline):
- `f32` (`BM_LogF32`, `BM_Log1pF32`): `-19.1%` on x86 AVX2+FMA3, `-28.8%` on x86 AVX-512, `-36.6%` on ARM64 NEON.
- `f64` (`BM_LogF64`, `BM_Log1pF64`): `1.7x-4.4x` faster across AVX2, AVX-512, and ARM64 NEON.

### Design choices

- Expose YNNPACK `log` and `log1p` wrappers for `f32` and `f64` vector widths up to 512 bits in `xla/codegen/intrinsic/cpp/ynnpack_unary.{h,cc}`, compile a single `ynnpack_unary_ll` bitcode library, inline from it during codegen, and stop splitting `v16f32` `log` on AVX-512.
- Keep upcasting `f16` and `bf16` to `f32`, since YNNPACK has no native full-precision 16-bit `log`/`log1p` kernels on x86.
- Preserve `log1p(-0.0) = -0.0` via `copysign`, and keep the existing `libm` and algebraic `Log1p` lowerings on GPU and when CppGen bitcode is unavailable.

### Compromises

Maximum error bounds in ULPs (from JAX's numerics test suite and `docs/accuracy.md`):

| Op | CPU (before) | CPU (this CL) | NVIDIA GPU | TPU (v6e / 7x) |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| `log` (`f32`) | 1.5 | 1.5 | 1.0 | 2.5 |
| `log` (`f64`) | 0.5 | 1.5 | 1.5 | N/A |
| `log1p` (`f32`) | 3.0 | 2.0 | 1.0 | 3.0 |
| `log1p` (`f64`) | 2.0 | 2.0 | 1.5 | N/A |
| `log10` (`f32`) | 3.0 | 2.5 | 2.5 | 3.0 |
| `logit` (`f32`) | 3.0 | 2.0 | 3.0 | 4.0 / 4.5 |
| `acosh` (`f32`) | 4.5 | 3.5 | 2.5 | 4.5 / 5.0 |
| `asinh` (`f32`) | 3.5 | 2.0 | 2.0 | 3.5 |
| `atanh` (`f32`) | 3.0 | 2.0 | 3.5 | 3.5 |

`f64` `log` trades scalar `libm`'s 0.5 ULP correct rounding for SIMD vectorization, matching GPU's 1.5 ULP bound (measured 1.23 ULP).

The `c128` `Log` exhaustive test gets a 1 ULP relative bound on CPU for inputs with tiny imaginary parts. CPU already flushes those imaginary parts to zero, which fails the distance check, so the real part `log|z|` was effectively held to exact `libm` results.

### Alternatives

- Tested a pure degree-8 Estrin polynomial (`Q = 1`) for `f32` `log` in YNNPACK, which avoided `fdiv` latency in isolation on wide AVX-512 vectors, but ran slower in XLA's unrolled elementwise loops across AVX2, AVX-512, and ARM64 NEON than the `[3/2]` rational kernel.
- Reaching `<= 1.0` ULP for both `log` and `log1p` requires split `ln(2)` plus double-word addition for `1 + x`, which added 18-68% per-vector overhead in microbenchmarks for accuracy tighter than GPU (`f64`) and TPU (`f32`).

### Updating tests

CPU `log` and `log1p` results move by about 1 ULP on many inputs, and by more in code that amplifies small differences (iterative solves, log-dets, KL divergences, derivatives). Tests that check exact equality, use tolerances below 1 ULP, or compare against goldens captured from the old output may fail. Please update them to allow a few ULP, or set goldens to exact reference values, rather than pinning bit-exact results.

display_title: [TF] Remove `rules_python_local_wheel.patch` in favor of `local_wheel_repo`.

head_commit.message:
[TF] Remove `rules_python_local_wheel.patch` in favor of `local_wheel_repo`.

Replace the `rules_python_local_wheel.patch` `single_version_override` and the
custom `pip.parse(local_wheels = ...)` attribute with a self-contained Starlark
repository rule (`local_wheel_repo` / `@local_tf_wheel`). Under Bzlmod,
`single_version_override` is ignored for non-root modules, so downstream
projects depending on TensorFlow via `MODULE.bazel` saw unpatched `rules_python`
and failed with `unknown attribute local_wheels provided`.

* Delete `third_party/py/rules_python_local_wheel.patch` and remove it along
  with `pip.parse(local_wheels = ...)` from `MODULE.bazel`.
* Add `third_party/extensions/local_wheel.bzl` (`local_wheel_repo`), a lazy,
  non-reproducible repository rule exposing `dist/<WHEEL_NAME>-*.whl` as
  `@local_tf_wheel//:whl` (watches `dist/` for incremental rebuilds, supports
  hyphen/underscore `WHEEL_NAME` variants, and safely produces an empty
  `filegroup` when `dist/` is absent).
* Update `tf_wheel_dep()` in `tensorflow/tools/pip_package/utils/tf_wheel.bzl`
  to return `@local_tf_wheel//:whl` under Bzlmod while keeping
  `@pypi//<WHEEL_NAME>:whl` under `--config=workspace`.

display_title: [XLA] Skip host-offload rematerialization of buffers with indirect uses

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Skip host-offload rematerialization of buffers with indirect uses

📝 Summary of Changes

HloRematerialization's host-offload strategy picks a candidate from the buffer-level user list that GetUsers builds from every position of the value, but OffloadInstruction then looks for the first unplaced user in the instruction's own users() to place the copy back to device before. The two lists differ when the value is also reached through another instruction's output, for example when it is forwarded into an async-start's output tuple and read by the async-done. If the only direct user (the async-start) is already placed, OffloadInstruction finds nothing and CHECK-fails: "Have nothing to place this before!".

This change makes GetCostOfHostOffload reject candidates whose buffer has indirect uses, the same rule the recompute strategy already applies (ExtendRecomputeBlock) for the same reason: the copy back can only be placed before a direct user. This is a bit broader than the crash: a value whose next use is a not yet placed async-start (or copy-start, send, collective start) is skipped too, as recompute already does; a narrower check would let the tracker free the buffer at the copy-start while a placed async-start still holds it.

GetCostOfCompression has the same gap (CompressInstruction would hit the empty-list CHECK in InsertBeforeInstructions), but it cannot trigger on GPU where no compact shape function is set, so I left it out of this change; happy to add the symmetric guard with a test if you want it here.

🎯 Justification

Fixes #51432. The module from the issue (a while body whose GEMM result feeds an asynchronous dynamic-update-slice) aborts GPU compilation at head with hlo-opt --platform=gpu --stage=hlo-backend and the a100_sxm_80 target spec when --xla_gpu_enable_host_memory_offloading=true. With this change it compiles (also with a100_sxm_40; h100_sxm never picked the candidate).

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests:

One new test in xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers/hlo_rematerialization_test.cc, OffloadingRematerializationTest.SkipOffloadWhenOnlyUserIsAsyncStart: a scheduled module where the only user of an add is an async-start placed right after it and the async-done is consumed at the end, with the same "hardware" constants as BasicSuccessfulHostOffload. Without the fix the test aborts on the CHECK; with it remat skips the add (which still feeds the async-start directly) and offloads the next candidate instead.

🧪 Execution Tests:

None added

display_title: PR #52878: [ROCM] Wire MORI ragged-all-to-all and all-gather through the GXL hook, add async start/done stubs

head_commit.message:
PR #52878: [ROCM] Wire MORI ragged-all-to-all and all-gather through the GXL hook, add async start/done stubs

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52878

## Summary

This change makes the MORI GPU collectives backend serve XLA's GXL
ragged-all-to-all / all-gather hook and adds async start/done support to the
MORI communicator, so ragged-all-to-all and other MORI collectives can be
issued on an async stream and overlapped by the latency-hiding scheduler.

It is gated behind the existing `--xla_gpu_enable_gxl_ragged_all_to_all` flag
and only takes effect when the collectives implementation is MORI
(`--xla_gpu_collectives_implementation=mori`); the default NCCL/RCCL path is
unchanged.

## Motivation

`RaggedAllToAllThunk` previously only had the symmetric-memory and peer-access
kernel strategies. MORI already implements a fast SDMA-push ragged-all-to-all
in the `CollectivesFacade`, but there was no way for the thunk to call into it.
I decided to reuse already existing `GxlCommunicator` interface (`RunAllGatherGxl`,
`RunRaggedAllToAllGxl`) for exactly this purpose, reached via
`GpuCommunicator::gxl_communicator()`. This PR implements that hook for MORI and
teaches the ragged-all-to-all thunk to delegate to it.

This way, we **do not need to add anything specific** to RaggedAllToAllThunk which is already quite complex.
There are just _two general fixes_ in RaggedAllToAllThunk related to GXL communicator handling.

## What changed

### GXL hook (`mori_communicator.{h,cc}`)

- `MoriCommunicator` now overrides `gxl_communicator()` and owns a nested
  `GxlAdapter` (a `GxlCommunicator` holding a back-pointer to the communicator).
  Using a member adapter rather than multiple inheritance keeps the
  `GpuCommunicator`/`GxlCommunicator` hierarchies separate.
- `GxlAdapter::RunAllGatherGxl` forwards to `LaunchAllGather`;
  `RunRaggedAllToAllGxl` forwards to the new `LaunchRaggedAllToAll`.

### Ragged-all-to-all thunk (`ragged_all_to_all_thunk.cc`)

- `Initialize`: when `enable_gxl` is set and the clique's communicator exposes a
  GXL communicator, return early — the GXL path runs the whole op, so no kernel
  or NCCL-fallback state is allocated (kernel strategy stays `kNone`).
- `Record`: under the same condition, delegate to `CollectiveThunk::Record`,
  which traces `RunCollective` and dispatches to the GXL communicator.

### Async start/done (`mori_communicator.{h,cc}`, `mori_kernels.h`)

- Added `SetAsync(bool)` / `AsyncDone(executor)` and an internal
  `LaunchOrDefer` helper. These is a preparation for MORI async collectives support, **not wired yet**.
- Removed the old `Execute` wrapper; the `Launch*` methods are called directly.

### Build / misc

- Renamed the MORI facade namespace usages from `mori::collective` to
  `mori::ccl` to match the repinned MORI headers.

### MORI repin (`third_party/roc_mori/workspace.bzl`)

- Repinned `@roc_mori` to MORI tag `xla-pin-20261112`
  (commit `d50338eb5f45d4338ee64ef27fa7f22a71638b9f`) with the matching archive
  `sha256`.

## Testing

- `RaggedAllToAll_2GPUs_CommandBuffer/async_nccl_fallback_peer` passes,
  exercising the async + command-buffer path end-to-end through the MORI GXL
  hook.
- Verified on a MaxText Mixtral-8x7b MoE run (expert-parallel, EP=8) that the
  MORI ragged-all-to-all kernel is selected and produces correct results; the
  collective runs at the standalone benchmark's bandwidth when ranks arrive
  together.

head_commit.message:
Chunk sub-byte sub-tile packing in tiled linearizer.

Linearizing sub-byte sub-tile-packed tensors previously allocated an unpacked host buffer spanning the entire array. Large sub-byte arrays caused tens of gigabytes of unreserved host memory growth.

display_title: Enable multi-subscriber graph trace attribute for CUPTI V2 graph-level tracing.

head_commit.message:
Enable multi-subscriber graph trace attribute for CUPTI V2 graph-level tracing.

When CUPTI V2 multi-subscriber mode (`allowMultipleSubscribers = 1`) is active (such as in CUDA 13.4 static CUPTI builds), enabling `CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_GRAPH_TRACE` via `cuptiActivityEnable_v2` returns `CUPTI_ERROR_MULTIPLE_SUBSCRIBERS_NOT_SUPPORTED` unless the global `CUPTI_ACTIVITY_ATTR_ENABLE_MULTI_SUBSCRIBER_GRAPH_TRACE` (`20`) attribute is set to `1` before enabling any activity kinds.

Set `CUPTI_ACTIVITY_ATTR_ENABLE_MULTI_SUBSCRIBER_GRAPH_TRACE` to `1` in `CuptiTracer::EnableActivityTracing` before calling `ActivityEnableV2` when `CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_GRAPH_TRACE` is selected, register an undo callback and `absl::Cleanup` so partial failures always restore `0`, and reset it to `0` in `CuptiTracer::DisableActivityTracing` after `ActivityFlushAll(CUPTI_ACTIVITY_FLAG_FLUSH_FORCED)` so subsequent node-level graph tracing sessions continue to receive per-node records. Also allow `CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED`, `CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_COMPATIBLE`, `CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_OPERATION`, and `CUPTI_ERROR_MULTIPLE_SUBSCRIBERS_NOT_SUPPORTED` in `CuptiErrorManager::ActivitySetAttributeV2`.

head_commit.message:
Migrate PjRt C API `MultiSliceConfig` wrappers to `xla::MultiSliceConfigRef`

Wrapping `xla::MultiSliceConfig` in `std::unique_ptr` inside
`PJRT_MultiSlice_Config` and the MegaScale C API client prevented C API
callers and plugins from sharing reference-counted `MultiSliceConfig`
ownership across the C/C++ boundary.

Store `xla::MultiSliceConfigRef` in `PJRT_MultiSlice_Config` and return
`xla::MultiSliceConfigRef` allocated via `tsl::MakeRef` from
`CreateAoTMegascaleConfig` and `CreateMultiSliceMegascaleConfig` in
`xla::megascale::c_api_client`, keeping a transitional `std::unique_ptr`
constructor on `PJRT_MultiSlice_Config` while plugin extensions migrate in
follow-up changes.

name: CI
display_title: PR #52878: [ROCM] Wire MORI ragged-all-to-all and all-gather through the GXL hook, add async start/done stubs

head_commit.message:
PR #52878: [ROCM] Wire MORI ragged-all-to-all and all-gather through the GXL hook, add async start/done stubs

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52878

## Summary

This change makes the MORI GPU collectives backend serve XLA's GXL
ragged-all-to-all / all-gather hook and adds async start/done support to the
MORI communicator, so ragged-all-to-all and other MORI collectives can be
issued on an async stream and overlapped by the latency-hiding scheduler.

It is gated behind the existing `--xla_gpu_enable_gxl_ragged_all_to_all` flag
and only takes effect when the collectives implementation is MORI
(`--xla_gpu_collectives_implementation=mori`); the default NCCL/RCCL path is
unchanged.

## Motivation

`RaggedAllToAllThunk` previously only had the symmetric-memory and peer-access
kernel strategies. MORI already implements a fast SDMA-push ragged-all-to-all
in the `CollectivesFacade`, but there was no way for the thunk to call into it.
I decided to reuse already existing `GxlCommunicator` interface (`RunAllGatherGxl`,
`RunRaggedAllToAllGxl`) for exactly this purpose, reached via
`GpuCommunicator::gxl_communicator()`. This PR implements that hook for MORI and
teaches the ragged-all-to-all thunk to delegate to it.

This way, we **do not need to add anything specific** to RaggedAllToAllThunk which is already quite complex.
There are just _two general fixes_ in RaggedAllToAllThunk related to GXL communicator handling.

## What changed

### GXL hook (`mori_communicator.{h,cc}`)

- `MoriCommunicator` now overrides `gxl_communicator()` and owns a nested
  `GxlAdapter` (a `GxlCommunicator` holding a back-pointer to the communicator).
  Using a member adapter rather than multiple inheritance keeps the
  `GpuCommunicator`/`GxlCommunicator` hierarchies separate.
- `GxlAdapter::RunAllGatherGxl` forwards to `LaunchAllGather`;
  `RunRaggedAllToAllGxl` forwards to the new `LaunchRaggedAllToAll`.

### Ragged-all-to-all thunk (`ragged_all_to_all_thunk.cc`)

- `Initialize`: when `enable_gxl` is set and the clique's communicator exposes a
  GXL communicator, return early — the GXL path runs the whole op, so no kernel
  or NCCL-fallback state is allocated (kernel strategy stays `kNone`).
- `Record`: under the same condition, delegate to `CollectiveThunk::Record`,
  which traces `RunCollective` and dispatches to the GXL communicator.

### Async start/done (`mori_communicator.{h,cc}`, `mori_kernels.h`)

- Added `SetAsync(bool)` / `AsyncDone(executor)` and an internal
  `LaunchOrDefer` helper. These is a preparation for MORI async collectives support, **not wired yet**.
- Removed the old `Execute` wrapper; the `Launch*` methods are called directly.

### Build / misc

- Renamed the MORI facade namespace usages from `mori::collective` to
  `mori::ccl` to match the repinned MORI headers.

### MORI repin (`third_party/roc_mori/workspace.bzl`)

- Repinned `@roc_mori` to MORI tag `xla-pin-20261112`
  (commit `d50338eb5f45d4338ee64ef27fa7f22a71638b9f`) with the matching archive
  `sha256`.

## Testing

- `RaggedAllToAll_2GPUs_CommandBuffer/async_nccl_fallback_peer` passes,
  exercising the async + command-buffer path end-to-end through the MORI GXL
  hook.
- Verified on a MaxText Mixtral-8x7b MoE run (expert-parallel, EP=8) that the
  MORI ragged-all-to-all kernel is selected and produces correct results; the
  collective runs at the standalone benchmark's bandwidth when ranks arrive
  together.

Linearizing sub-byte sub-tile-packed tensors previously allocated an unpacked host buffer spanning the entire array. Large sub-byte arrays caused tens of gigabytes of unreserved host memory growth.

This change transposes and repacks sub-byte host-to-device data in bounded megabyte-scale chunks above the scratch threshold. Each chunk reuses small scratch storage and uses parallel transpose execution whenever the chunk plan exposes parallelism.

[PJRT] Clear PadRealToStatic prefix through embedded offload dispatchers

Offload passes can move `PadRealToStatic` into async or called subcomputations,
including behind embedded root custom-call dispatchers where
`HloDataflowAnalysis` stops. Trace `PadRealToStatic` operands across those
boundaries so PJRT clears the entry parameter metadata prefix and rejects
shared, returned, or aliased uses.

Migrate PjRt C API `MultiSliceConfig` wrappers to `xla::MultiSliceConfigRef`

Wrapping `xla::MultiSliceConfig` in `std::unique_ptr` inside
`PJRT_MultiSlice_Config` and the MegaScale C API client prevented C API
callers and plugins from sharing reference-counted `MultiSliceConfig`
ownership across the C/C++ boundary.

Store `xla::MultiSliceConfigRef` in `PJRT_MultiSlice_Config` and return
`xla::MultiSliceConfigRef` allocated via `tsl::MakeRef` from
`CreateAoTMegascaleConfig` and `CreateMultiSliceMegascaleConfig` in
`xla::megascale::c_api_client`, keeping a transitional `std::unique_ptr`
constructor on `PJRT_MultiSlice_Config` while plugin extensions migrate in
follow-up changes.

display_title: Hoist stride-1 minor dimension out of BroadcastHelper inner loop in literal.cc.

head_commit.message:
Hoist stride-1 minor dimension out of BroadcastHelper inner loop in literal.cc.

BroadcastHelper previously invoked IndexUtil::MultidimensionalIndexToLinearIndex
and IndexUtil::BumpIndices on every output element, even along the contiguous
stride-1 most-minor layout dimension. Hoist result_minor_to_major[0] out of
broadcast_shape and fill inner_broadcast_size contiguous elements directly (via
memset for 1-byte elements and a contiguous memcpy loop otherwise), yielding a
1.52x geomean speedup across literal broadcast/populate benchmarks (14.24x on
BM_BroadcastVectorToMatrix/16/1024).

display_title: PR #52878: [ROCM] Wire MORI ragged-all-to-all and all-gather through the GXL hook, add async start/done stubs

head_commit.message:
PR #52878: [ROCM] Wire MORI ragged-all-to-all and all-gather through the GXL hook, add async start/done stubs

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52878

## Summary

This change makes the MORI GPU collectives backend serve XLA's GXL
ragged-all-to-all / all-gather hook and adds async start/done support to the
MORI communicator, so ragged-all-to-all and other MORI collectives can be
issued on an async stream and overlapped by the latency-hiding scheduler.

It is gated behind the existing `--xla_gpu_enable_gxl_ragged_all_to_all` flag
and only takes effect when the collectives implementation is MORI
(`--xla_gpu_collectives_implementation=mori`); the default NCCL/RCCL path is
unchanged.

## Motivation

`RaggedAllToAllThunk` previously only had the symmetric-memory and peer-access
kernel strategies. MORI already implements a fast SDMA-push ragged-all-to-all
in the `CollectivesFacade`, but there was no way for the thunk to call into it.
I decided to reuse already existing `GxlCommunicator` interface (`RunAllGatherGxl`,
`RunRaggedAllToAllGxl`) for exactly this purpose, reached via
`GpuCommunicator::gxl_communicator()`. This PR implements that hook for MORI and
teaches the ragged-all-to-all thunk to delegate to it.

This way, we **do not need to add anything specific** to RaggedAllToAllThunk which is already quite complex.
There are just _two general fixes_ in RaggedAllToAllThunk related to GXL communicator handling.

## What changed

### GXL hook (`mori_communicator.{h,cc}`)

- `MoriCommunicator` now overrides `gxl_communicator()` and owns a nested
  `GxlAdapter` (a `GxlCommunicator` holding a back-pointer to the communicator).
  Using a member adapter rather than multiple inheritance keeps the
  `GpuCommunicator`/`GxlCommunicator` hierarchies separate.
- `GxlAdapter::RunAllGatherGxl` forwards to `LaunchAllGather`;
  `RunRaggedAllToAllGxl` forwards to the new `LaunchRaggedAllToAll`.

### Ragged-all-to-all thunk (`ragged_all_to_all_thunk.cc`)

- `Initialize`: when `enable_gxl` is set and the clique's communicator exposes a
  GXL communicator, return early — the GXL path runs the whole op, so no kernel
  or NCCL-fallback state is allocated (kernel strategy stays `kNone`).
- `Record`: under the same condition, delegate to `CollectiveThunk::Record`,
  which traces `RunCollective` and dispatches to the GXL communicator.

### Async start/done (`mori_communicator.{h,cc}`, `mori_kernels.h`)

- Added `SetAsync(bool)` / `AsyncDone(executor)` and an internal
  `LaunchOrDefer` helper. These is a preparation for MORI async collectives support, **not wired yet**.
- Removed the old `Execute` wrapper; the `Launch*` methods are called directly.

### Build / misc

- Renamed the MORI facade namespace usages from `mori::collective` to
  `mori::ccl` to match the repinned MORI headers.

### MORI repin (`third_party/roc_mori/workspace.bzl`)

- Repinned `@roc_mori` to MORI tag `xla-pin-20261112`
  (commit `d50338eb5f45d4338ee64ef27fa7f22a71638b9f`) with the matching archive
  `sha256`.

## Testing

- `RaggedAllToAll_2GPUs_CommandBuffer/async_nccl_fallback_peer` passes,
  exercising the async + command-buffer path end-to-end through the MORI GXL
  hook.
- Verified on a MaxText Mixtral-8x7b MoE run (expert-parallel, EP=8) that the
  MORI ragged-all-to-all kernel is selected and produces correct results; the
  collective runs at the standalone benchmark's bandwidth when ranks arrive
  together.

display_title: [TF] Remove `rules_python_local_wheel.patch` in favor of `local_wheel_repo`.

head_commit.message:
[TF] Remove `rules_python_local_wheel.patch` in favor of `local_wheel_repo`.

Replace the `rules_python_local_wheel.patch` `single_version_override` and the
custom `pip.parse(local_wheels = ...)` attribute with a self-contained Starlark
repository rule (`local_wheel_repo` / `@local_tf_wheel`). Under Bzlmod,
`single_version_override` is ignored for non-root modules, so downstream
projects depending on TensorFlow via `MODULE.bazel` saw unpatched `rules_python`
and failed with `unknown attribute local_wheels provided`.

* Delete `third_party/py/rules_python_local_wheel.patch` and remove it along
  with `pip.parse(local_wheels = ...)` from `MODULE.bazel`.
* Add `third_party/extensions/local_wheel.bzl` (`local_wheel_repo`), a lazy,
  non-reproducible repository rule exposing `dist/<WHEEL_NAME>-*.whl` as
  `@local_tf_wheel//:whl` (watches `dist/` for incremental rebuilds, supports
  hyphen/underscore `WHEEL_NAME` variants, and safely produces an empty
  `filegroup` when `dist/` is absent).
* Update `tf_wheel_dep()` in `tensorflow/tools/pip_package/utils/tf_wheel.bzl`
  to return `@local_tf_wheel//:whl` under Bzlmod while keeping
  `@pypi//<WHEEL_NAME>:whl` under `--config=workspace`.

***Problem:*** Unaligned vector transfer lowering and scalar elementwise shared-memory extraction split 32-bit packed loads and stores into narrow memory operations, inflate sub-byte vector SelectionDAG legalization, and under-occupy packed transpose blocks.

***Solution:*** Infer byte alignment from base buffers and affine index divisors, lower aligned power-of-two sub-byte vector transfers through wide integer loads and stores, and transpose 32-bit packed shared-memory tiles with an in-register `i32` butterfly at 256 threads per block.

display_title: PR #52878: [ROCM] Wire MORI ragged-all-to-all and all-gather through the GXL hook, add async start/done stubs

head_commit.message:
PR #52878: [ROCM] Wire MORI ragged-all-to-all and all-gather through the GXL hook, add async start/done stubs

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52878

## Summary

This change makes the MORI GPU collectives backend serve XLA's GXL
ragged-all-to-all / all-gather hook and adds async start/done support to the
MORI communicator, so ragged-all-to-all and other MORI collectives can be
issued on an async stream and overlapped by the latency-hiding scheduler.

It is gated behind the existing `--xla_gpu_enable_gxl_ragged_all_to_all` flag
and only takes effect when the collectives implementation is MORI
(`--xla_gpu_collectives_implementation=mori`); the default NCCL/RCCL path is
unchanged.

## Motivation

`RaggedAllToAllThunk` previously only had the symmetric-memory and peer-access
kernel strategies. MORI already implements a fast SDMA-push ragged-all-to-all
in the `CollectivesFacade`, but there was no way for the thunk to call into it.
I decided to reuse already existing `GxlCommunicator` interface (`RunAllGatherGxl`,
`RunRaggedAllToAllGxl`) for exactly this purpose, reached via
`GpuCommunicator::gxl_communicator()`. This PR implements that hook for MORI and
teaches the ragged-all-to-all thunk to delegate to it.

This way, we **do not need to add anything specific** to RaggedAllToAllThunk which is already quite complex.
There are just _two general fixes_ in RaggedAllToAllThunk related to GXL communicator handling.

## What changed

### GXL hook (`mori_communicator.{h,cc}`)

- `MoriCommunicator` now overrides `gxl_communicator()` and owns a nested
  `GxlAdapter` (a `GxlCommunicator` holding a back-pointer to the communicator).
  Using a member adapter rather than multiple inheritance keeps the
  `GpuCommunicator`/`GxlCommunicator` hierarchies separate.
- `GxlAdapter::RunAllGatherGxl` forwards to `LaunchAllGather`;
  `RunRaggedAllToAllGxl` forwards to the new `LaunchRaggedAllToAll`.

### Ragged-all-to-all thunk (`ragged_all_to_all_thunk.cc`)

- `Initialize`: when `enable_gxl` is set and the clique's communicator exposes a
  GXL communicator, return early — the GXL path runs the whole op, so no kernel
  or NCCL-fallback state is allocated (kernel strategy stays `kNone`).
- `Record`: under the same condition, delegate to `CollectiveThunk::Record`,
  which traces `RunCollective` and dispatches to the GXL communicator.

### Async start/done (`mori_communicator.{h,cc}`, `mori_kernels.h`)

- Added `SetAsync(bool)` / `AsyncDone(executor)` and an internal
  `LaunchOrDefer` helper. These is a preparation for MORI async collectives support, **not wired yet**.
- Removed the old `Execute` wrapper; the `Launch*` methods are called directly.

### Build / misc

- Renamed the MORI facade namespace usages from `mori::collective` to
  `mori::ccl` to match the repinned MORI headers.

### MORI repin (`third_party/roc_mori/workspace.bzl`)

- Repinned `@roc_mori` to MORI tag `xla-pin-20261112`
  (commit `d50338eb5f45d4338ee64ef27fa7f22a71638b9f`) with the matching archive
  `sha256`.

## Testing

- `RaggedAllToAll_2GPUs_CommandBuffer/async_nccl_fallback_peer` passes,
  exercising the async + command-buffer path end-to-end through the MORI GXL
  hook.
- Verified on a MaxText Mixtral-8x7b MoE run (expert-parallel, EP=8) that the
  MORI ragged-all-to-all kernel is selected and produces correct results; the
  collective runs at the standalone benchmark's bandwidth when ranks arrive
  together.

display_title: [XLA] Handle late bound async-start DUS in the async chain output path

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Handle late bound async-start DUS in the async chain output path

Dataflow analysis crashes on a late bound `async-start` wrapping `dynamic-update-slice`. Such a start has no operands; its operands and output are bound on the `async-update`. `UpdateAsyncStartValueSet` special cased DUS starts and read `operand(0)` without checking that it exists.

The DUS case moves into `UpdateAsyncChainOutputValueSet`. A DUS start still forwards its destination operand to `{1}`, but only when the start has that operand; otherwise it falls back to the wrapped root and the existing bound checks skip the unbound output. The forwarding is required: without it, a loop carried DUS start feeds the wrapped result back into the shared destination parameter, which then has two values and fails in place aliasing.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1020158276

instruction, or effective scalar constants that compare less than or
equal.

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Cap the number of operands of a loop fusion

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Cap the number of operands of a loop fusion

`CpuInstructionFusion` has no bound on how large a loop fusion may grow. The only size-related guard, `FusionNodeIndexingEvaluation::CodeDuplicationTooHigh`, is skipped entirely when the pass runs with `may_duplicate=false`, which `cpu_compiler.cc` selects whenever `xla_cpu_use_multi_output_fusion` is set.

On reverse-mode AD programs of stencil codes (Enzyme-MLIR / Reactant differentiating the Oceananigans ocean model) this produces loop fusions with 210–250 operands and 880–1045 fused instructions per output element: the `pad`-accumulate chain of every halo'd adjoint pulls in each stencil tap's whole producer DAG. The elemental emitter's per-element code for such a fusion neither vectorizes nor fits in registers; the reverse loop ran ~10× the primal while doing 4.2× its FLOPs.

This change adds an operand budget, checked independently of `may_duplicate()`: a producer is not fused into an existing fusion if the result would have more than `xla_cpu_max_fusion_operands` distinct operands (default 96, matching the GPU backend's `MaxOperandsAndOutputsPerFusion`). The option is an `xla_backend_extra_options` entry read through `cpu_options`; a value `<= 0` disables the check.

The budget is deliberately on operands only. An earlier revision also capped the number of fused instructions (512), which split long single-input elementwise chains and changed numerics in two JAX CPU tests: (a) `jax.scipy.special.iv` (f32) is a 540-instruction chain using double-float arithmetic; XLA:CPU sets `contract` on all FP arithmetic, so a kernel boundary prevents FMA contraction across it and breaks the error-free transformations (1.36 ULP instead of ≤ 1). (b) `ndtri_exp` gradient (bf16) differs on subnormal inputs: XLA:CPU runs kernels with denormals-are-zero, but LLVM folds `y == 0` on a bf16→f32 convert into an integer test on the bits, while `y < 0` stays a `ucomiss` that honors DAZ; which fold applies depends on the kernel boundaries. Both effects are pre-existing properties of XLA:CPU that any change in fusion boundaries can expose; the operand cap alone does not split these chains (they have 1–13 operands) and does not change either test.

Measurements (Oceananigans channel-model gradient, 8 time steps, one x86 core, `xla_cpu_use_multi_output_fusion` on; min / median of 3 calls):

| operand cap | gradient | primal |
|---|---|---|
| unpatched | 28.1 / 28.9 s | 3.01 s |
| disabled (`0`, control) | 28.0 / 29.3 s | — |
| 128 | 17.4 / 17.7 s | — |
| 96 (default) | 13.8 / 14.2 s | 2.89 s |
| 64 | 14.8 / 14.9 s | — |
| 48 | 11.7–13.1 / 12.2–13.2 s | 2.37 s |
| 32 | 12.8 / 13.1 s | 2.19 s |

(The 48 row spans four runs with the earlier instruction cap at 512, 1024, 4096 and disabled: 13.0, 11.7, 12.8, 13.1 s min — the instruction cap had no measurable effect, which is why it was dropped.) Results are bit-identical in the objective and agree with the unpatched build to rel. L2 ≤ 2e-15 in every gradient field.

The default is 96 rather than 48 based on a sweep over a suite of 80 CPU benchmark HLO models (A/B against head, 20 runs each). Compiling every model at several caps shows that any cap from 48 to 128 changes the fused HLO of the same two models (every other model has at most 42 operands per fusion), whereas the TORAX plasma-simulation models have fusions of 49–267 operands and are sensitive to the exact value: at cap 48 three of them regress 2–5% in wall time on Granite Rapids (4–13% on AMD Rome), while at cap 96 none regresses by more than 1% and their geomean improves by 1.2% (Granite Rapids) / 2.6% (Rome). The two models affected at any cap are within ±2% at either value. Suite-wide, the cap leaves runtime unchanged (geomean −0.2%) and improves compile wall time by 2% at the cost of 2% more compile CPU time.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:CPU] Cap the number of operands of a loop fusion

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Cap the number of operands of a loop fusion

`CpuInstructionFusion` has no bound on how large a loop fusion may grow. The only size-related guard, `FusionNodeIndexingEvaluation::CodeDuplicationTooHigh`, is skipped entirely when the pass runs with `may_duplicate=false`, which `cpu_compiler.cc` selects whenever `xla_cpu_use_multi_output_fusion` is set.

On reverse-mode AD programs of stencil codes (Enzyme-MLIR / Reactant differentiating the Oceananigans ocean model) this produces loop fusions with 210–250 operands and 880–1045 fused instructions per output element: the `pad`-accumulate chain of every halo'd adjoint pulls in each stencil tap's whole producer DAG. The elemental emitter's per-element code for such a fusion neither vectorizes nor fits in registers; the reverse loop ran ~10× the primal while doing 4.2× its FLOPs.

This change adds an operand budget, checked independently of `may_duplicate()`: a producer is not fused into an existing fusion if the result would have more than `xla_cpu_max_fusion_operands` distinct operands (default 96, matching the GPU backend's `MaxOperandsAndOutputsPerFusion`). The option is an `xla_backend_extra_options` entry read through `cpu_options`; a value `<= 0` disables the check.

The budget is deliberately on operands only. An earlier revision also capped the number of fused instructions (512), which split long single-input elementwise chains and changed numerics in two JAX CPU tests: (a) `jax.scipy.special.iv` (f32) is a 540-instruction chain using double-float arithmetic; XLA:CPU sets `contract` on all FP arithmetic, so a kernel boundary prevents FMA contraction across it and breaks the error-free transformations (1.36 ULP instead of ≤ 1). (b) `ndtri_exp` gradient (bf16) differs on subnormal inputs: XLA:CPU runs kernels with denormals-are-zero, but LLVM folds `y == 0` on a bf16→f32 convert into an integer test on the bits, while `y < 0` stays a `ucomiss` that honors DAZ; which fold applies depends on the kernel boundaries. Both effects are pre-existing properties of XLA:CPU that any change in fusion boundaries can expose; the operand cap alone does not split these chains (they have 1–13 operands) and does not change either test.

Measurements (Oceananigans channel-model gradient, 8 time steps, one x86 core, `xla_cpu_use_multi_output_fusion` on; min / median of 3 calls):

| operand cap | gradient | primal |
|---|---|---|
| unpatched | 28.1 / 28.9 s | 3.01 s |
| disabled (`0`, control) | 28.0 / 29.3 s | — |
| 128 | 17.4 / 17.7 s | — |
| 96 (default) | 13.8 / 14.2 s | 2.89 s |
| 64 | 14.8 / 14.9 s | — |
| 48 | 11.7–13.1 / 12.2–13.2 s | 2.37 s |
| 32 | 12.8 / 13.1 s | 2.19 s |

(The 48 row spans four runs with the earlier instruction cap at 512, 1024, 4096 and disabled: 13.0, 11.7, 12.8, 13.1 s min — the instruction cap had no measurable effect, which is why it was dropped.) Results are bit-identical in the objective and agree with the unpatched build to rel. L2 ≤ 2e-15 in every gradient field.

The default is 96 rather than 48 based on a sweep over a suite of 80 CPU benchmark HLO models (A/B against head, 20 runs each). Compiling every model at several caps shows that any cap from 48 to 128 changes the fused HLO of the same two models (every other model has at most 42 operands per fusion), whereas the TORAX plasma-simulation models have fusions of 49–267 operands and are sensitive to the exact value: at cap 48 three of them regress 2–5% in wall time on Granite Rapids (4–13% on AMD Rome), while at cap 96 none regresses by more than 1% and their geomean improves by 1.2% (Granite Rapids) / 2.6% (Rome). The two models affected at any cap are within ±2% at either value. Suite-wide, the cap leaves runtime unchanged (geomean −0.2%) and improves compile wall time by 2% at the cost of 2% more compile CPU time.

Tests: `cpu_instruction_fusion_test` gains five cases on a 120-tap pad/add chain: the default budget splits it (largest fusion exactly 96 operands), also with `may_duplicate=false`, the budget is configurable (16), disabling it fuses the whole chain into one fusion, and a malformed option value is rejected with `InvalidArgument`.

name: CI
display_title: [ROCm] Fix ROCm multi-GPU CI failures.

head_commit.message:
[ROCm] Fix ROCm multi-GPU CI failures.

 - RcclCommunicator had no LaunchReduce; CollectiveReduce runtime support
   was added for NCCL only. Implemented on top of ncclReduce.
 - Backend::CreateGpuAllocators registered no collective memory space
   allocator, so any module whose device count equals the visible device
   count died with "No allocator found ... memory space 7" once buffer
   assignment colored its temp buffer S(7). Not ROCm specific.
 - MORI dlopen()s amd_smi by unversioned name and exit(-1)s when that
   fails, which no hermetic ROCm build can satisfy; XLA now hands it the
   path of the copy already mapped into the process.
 - ShardedAutotuningWorks hard-coded TCP port 12345 and failed when an
   unrelated process held it; it now picks a free port.
 - Symmetric-memory ragged-all-to-all needs a
   NCCL LSA window; it is CUDA-only and has no RCCL equivalent.
 - Command-buffer control flow and cross-host
   disabled on ROCm by CommandBufferConversionPass and IsLsaPossible().

name: CI
display_title: Bound the traversal of MLIR locations when exporting them to HLO metadata.

head_commit.message:
Bound the traversal of MLIR locations when exporting them to HLO metadata.

MLIR uniques locations, so nested locations (`CallSiteLoc`, `FusedLoc`,
`NameLoc`) can share sub-locations and form a DAG. The MHLO to HLO export
walked such locations recursively as trees when building op names, stack frames,
and source file/line metadata. With shared sub-locations, the work and the size
of the exported metadata grew exponentially with the nesting depth, and deeply
nested locations could overflow the C++ call stack.

Convert these traversals to iterative worklists, visit at most 4096 locations
per exported location, and cap the exported `op_name` at 4096 bytes by dropping
the names that do not fit. Locations emitted by frontends are far smaller, so
their metadata is unchanged; only pathologically nested or oversized locations
get truncated metadata. Empty names are now skipped instead of adding a
separator to the `op_name`.

Shared sub-locations are still visited every time they occur instead of being
deduplicated, because repeated locations are legitimate, for example the stack
frames of a recursive function.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] HostOffloader: do not follow tokens when walking host memory offload paths

head_commit.message:
[XLA] HostOffloader: do not follow tokens when walking host memory offload paths

📝 Summary of Changes

HostOffloader::WalkDownHostMemoryOffloadPaths follows the offloaded buffer through its users. For a generic user it keeps the same shape index, so a send user is tracked as the whole send result tuple, its send-done user is tracked as a token, and if that token is returned from the entry computation the pass ends up in the output streaming check, which does CHECK(leaf.has_layout()) on the entry result leaves. Tokens never have a layout, so the compiler aborts.

A token carries no data, so an offloaded buffer never flows through it (send-done only produces a token; the data stays in send's output {0}). This change skips token-shaped successors in the walk, and makes the output streaming check skip non-array leaves (the send result tuple itself has a token leaf, so returning the send from the entry computation hit the same CHECK). Arrays and tuples are handled exactly as before, and the existing send test (BasicHostTransferSendNoCrash) still gets its copy to host memory in front of the send.

🎯 Justification

Fixes #50971. The module from the issue (MoveToHost -> send -> send-done -> ROOT tuple(send-done)) aborts GPU compilation at HEAD with "Check failed: leaf.has_layout() Expecting output shape of entry computation to have a layout." With this change it gets the same clean error as the module without the MoveToHost ("Expected recv to match send", the fuzzer module has no matching recv), and a properly paired program compiles normally.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests:

Two new tests in xla/hlo/transforms/host_offloader_test.cc. SendDoneTokenReturnedFromEntryNoCrash runs the pass on the issue's module and checks that it succeeds, that the root is still tuple(send-done(send(copy(param), after-all))), that the copy is in host memory and the parameter is not, and that no annotations remain. SendResultReturnedFromEntryNoCrash returns the send itself from the entry computation and expects a clean error (the offloaded data would be returned in a device memory output). Without the source change both tests abort with the CHECK from the issue.

🧪 Execution Tests:

None added. Checked manually with run_hlo_module

name: CI
display_title: PR #52161: [ROCm] Add a temp buffer pool for --xla_gpu_temp_buffer_use_separate_color

head_commit.message:
PR #52161: [ROCm] Add a temp buffer pool for --xla_gpu_temp_buffer_use_separate_color

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52161

ROCm only change, This is to help us get stable address which we can use to avoid collective recapture whenever stable address is there.

## 📝 Summary of Changes

On ROCm, `--xla_gpu_temp_buffer_use_separate_color` gets a separate, non-preallocated BFC pool per device for memory space `kTempBuffer`. Next to a preallocated default pool it may use the device memory that the default pool's memory fraction leaves, like the collective pool. without preallocation it has the default pool's limit.

## 🎯 Justification

The flag assigns temp buffers to `kTempBuffer`, but only CUDA registered an allocator for that space. On ROCm, an executable whose temp allocations are combined fails:

```
INTERNAL: No allocator found in MultiDeviceAdapter for device ordinal 0 and memory space 2
```

Only temp buffers use the new pool, so each execution gets the same temp address, which is what the flag is for.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Verify the reduction dimensions against the input in CudnnNormRewriter.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Verify the reduction dimensions against the input in CudnnNormRewriter.

When matching a layer norm pattern, the operand of the reduction that calculates
the expectation may differ from the layer norm input by a reshape or bitcast
that adds or removes degenerate dimensions. `MatchLayerNorm` nevertheless used
the dimensions of the reduction to index into the shape of the input when
deriving the transpose order and the shape of the cuDNN operands. If the
reduction's operand had a higher rank than the input, this resulted in
out-of-bounds accesses of the inverse transpose order and of the input's
dimensions.

The rewrite is now skipped unless all reduction dimensions are valid dimensions
of the input and select the same non-degenerate dimensions in the input as in
the reduction's operand. Patterns for which the dimensions agree are still
rewritten.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1020112237

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Cap the number of operands of a loop fusion

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Cap the number of operands of a loop fusion

`CpuInstructionFusion` has no bound on how large a loop fusion may grow. The only size-related guard, `FusionNodeIndexingEvaluation::CodeDuplicationTooHigh`, is skipped entirely when the pass runs with `may_duplicate=false`, which `cpu_compiler.cc` selects whenever `xla_cpu_use_multi_output_fusion` is set.

On reverse-mode AD programs of stencil codes (Enzyme-MLIR / Reactant differentiating the Oceananigans ocean model) this produces loop fusions with 210–250 operands and 880–1045 fused instructions per output element: the `pad`-accumulate chain of every halo'd adjoint pulls in each stencil tap's whole producer DAG. The elemental emitter's per-element code for such a fusion neither vectorizes nor fits in registers; the reverse loop ran ~10× the primal while doing 4.2× its FLOPs.

This change adds an operand budget, checked independently of `may_duplicate()`: a producer is not fused into an existing fusion if the result would have more than `xla_cpu_max_fusion_operands` distinct operands (default 96, matching the GPU backend's `MaxOperandsAndOutputsPerFusion`). The option is an `xla_backend_extra_options` entry read through `cpu_options`; a value `<= 0` disables the check.

The budget is deliberately on operands only. An earlier revision also capped the number of fused instructions (512), which split long single-input elementwise chains and changed numerics in two JAX CPU tests: (a) `jax.scipy.special.iv` (f32) is a 540-instruction chain using double-float arithmetic; XLA:CPU sets `contract` on all FP arithmetic, so a kernel boundary prevents FMA contraction across it and breaks the error-free transformations (1.36 ULP instead of ≤ 1). (b) `ndtri_exp` gradient (bf16) differs on subnormal inputs: XLA:CPU runs kernels with denormals-are-zero, but LLVM folds `y == 0` on a bf16→f32 convert into an integer test on the bits, while `y < 0` stays a `ucomiss` that honors DAZ; which fold applies depends on the kernel boundaries. Both effects are pre-existing properties of XLA:CPU that any change in fusion boundaries can expose; the operand cap alone does not split these chains (they have 1–13 operands) and does not change either test.

Measurements (Oceananigans channel-model gradient, 8 time steps, one x86 core, `xla_cpu_use_multi_output_fusion` on; min / median of 3 calls):

| operand cap | gradient | primal |
|---|---|---|
| unpatched | 28.1 / 28.9 s | 3.01 s |
| disabled (`0`, control) | 28.0 / 29.3 s | — |
| 128 | 17.4 / 17.7 s | — |
| 96 (default) | 13.8 / 14.2 s | 2.89 s |
| 64 | 14.8 / 14.9 s | — |
| 48 | 11.7–13.1 / 12.2–13.2 s | 2.37 s |
| 32 | 12.8 / 13.1 s | 2.19 s |

(The 48 row spans four runs with the earlier instruction cap at 512, 1024, 4096 and disabled: 13.0, 11.7, 12.8, 13.1 s min — the instruction cap had no measurable effect, which is why it was dropped.) Results are bit-identical in the objective and agree with the unpatched build to rel. L2 ≤ 2e-15 in every gradient field.

The default is 96 rather than 48 based on a sweep over a suite of 80 CPU benchmark HLO models (A/B against head, 20 runs each). Compiling every model at several caps shows that any cap from 48 to 128 changes the fused HLO of the same two models (every other model has at most 42 operands per fusion), whereas the TORAX plasma-simulation models have fusions of 49–267 operands and are sensitive to the exact value: at cap 48 three of them regress 2–5% in wall time on Granite Rapids (4–13% on AMD Rome), while at cap 96 none regresses by more than 1% and their geomean improves by 1.2% (Granite Rapids) / 2.6% (Rome). The two models affected at any cap are within ±2% at either value. Suite-wide, the cap leaves runtime unchanged (geomean −0.2%) and improves compile wall time by 2% at the cost of 2% more compile CPU time.

Tests: `cpu_instruction_fusion_test` gains five cases on a 120-tap pad/add chain: the default budget splits it (largest fusion exactly 96 operands), also with `may_duplicate=false`, the budget is configurable (16), disabling it fuses the whole chain into one fusion, and a malformed option value is rejected with `InvalidArgument`.

The same change is vendored as a patch in Enzyme-JAX (https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Enzyme-JAX/pull/3882, https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Enzyme-JAX/pull/3883).

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Handle late bound async-start DUS in the async chain output path

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Handle late bound async-start DUS in the async chain output path

Dataflow analysis crashes on a late bound `async-start` wrapping `dynamic-update-slice`. Such a start has no operands; its operands and output are bound on the `async-update`. `UpdateAsyncStartValueSet` special cased DUS starts and read `operand(0)` without checking that it exists.

The DUS case moves into `UpdateAsyncChainOutputValueSet`. A DUS start still forwards its destination operand to `{1}`, but only when the start has that operand; otherwise it falls back to the wrapped root and the existing bound checks skip the unbound output. The forwarding is required: without it, a loop carried DUS start feeds the wrapped result back into the shared destination parameter, which then has two values and fails in place aliasing.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1018504350

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fix sub-byte operand read bytes and batched dot shared-memory sizing.

Fusion operand read estimation previously rounded each element up to whole
bytes, overcounting tiled read bytes and L2 read traffic by 2x on bit-packed
4-bit quantized operands (assuming sub-byte operands are packed in memory).
Meanwhile, per-block dot shared-memory sizing omitted the batch tile multiplier
(`b > 1`), truncated odd bit totals via floor division by 8, and sized `pred`
tiles at 1 bit instead of 8-bit storage width.

An earlier revision also capped the number of fused instructions (512), which split long single-input elementwise chains and changed numerics in two JAX CPU tests: (a) `jax.scipy.special.iv` (f32) is a 540-instruction chain using double-float arithmetic; XLA:CPU sets `contract` on all FP arithmetic, so a kernel boundary prevents FMA contraction across it and breaks the error-free transformations (1.36 ULP instead of ≤ 1). (b) `ndtri_exp` gradient (bf16) differs on subnormal inputs: XLA:CPU runs kernels with denormals-are-zero, but LLVM folds `y == 0` on a bf16→f32 convert into an integer test on the bits, while `y < 0` stays a `ucomiss` that honors DAZ; which fold applies depends on the kernel boundaries. Both effects are pre-existing properties of XLA:CPU that any change in fusion boundaries can expose; the operand cap alone does not split these chains (they have 1–13 operands) and does not change either test.

Measurements (Oceananigans channel-model gradient, 8 time steps, one x86 core, `xla_cpu_use_multi_output_fusion` on; min / median of 3 calls):

| operand cap | gradient | primal |
|---|---|---|
| unpatched | 28.1 / 28.9 s | 3.01 s |
| disabled (`0`, control) | 28.0 / 29.3 s | — |
| 128 | 17.4 / 17.7 s | — |
| 96 (default) | 13.8 / 14.2 s | 2.89 s |
| 64 | 14.8 / 14.9 s | — |
| 48 | 11.7–13.1 / 12.2–13.2 s | 2.37 s |
| 32 | 12.8 / 13.1 s | 2.19 s |

(The 48 row spans four runs with the earlier instruction cap at 512, 1024, 4096 and disabled: 13.0, 11.7, 12.8, 13.1 s min — the instruction cap had no measurable effect, which is why it was dropped.) Results are bit-identical in the objective and agree with the unpatched build to rel. L2 ≤ 2e-15 in every gradient field.

The default is 96 rather than 48 based on a sweep over a suite of 80 CPU benchmark HLO models (A/B against head, 20 runs each). Compiling every model at several caps shows that any cap from 48 to 128 changes the fused HLO of the same two models (every other model has at most 42 operands per fusion), whereas the TORAX plasma-simulation models have fusions of 49–267 operands and are sensitive to the exact value: at cap 48 three of them regress 2–5% in wall time on Granite Rapids (4–13% on AMD Rome), while at cap 96 none regresses by more than 1% and their geomean improves by 1.2% (Granite Rapids) / 2.6% (Rome). The two models affected at any cap are within ±2% at either value. Suite-wide, the cap leaves runtime unchanged (geomean −0.2%) and improves compile wall time by 2% at the cost of 2% more compile CPU time.

Tests: `cpu_instruction_fusion_test` gains five cases on a 120-tap pad/add chain: the default budget splits it (largest fusion exactly 96 operands), also with `may_duplicate=false`, the budget is configurable (16), disabling it fuses the whole chain into one fusion, and a malformed option value is rejected with `InvalidArgument`.

The same change is vendored as a patch in Enzyme-JAX (https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Enzyme-JAX/pull/3882, https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Enzyme-JAX/pull/3883).

name: CI
display_title: Validate original value shape indices when deserializing HLO instructions

head_commit.message:
Validate original value shape indices when deserializing HLO instructions

`HloInstruction::CreateFromProto` passed the shape indices of an
`OriginalValueProto` to `OriginalValue::FromProto` without checking them
against the shape of the instruction. The tuple tree built from these indices
grows with the magnitude and the length of the indices, so a small malformed
proto could cause excessive memory allocation or very deep recursion before
the HLO verifier had a chance to run.

`HloInstruction::CreateFromProto` now returns an `InvalidArgument` error if an
element of the original value has a shape index that does not exist in the
shape of the instruction, which bounds the size of the tree by the size of the
shape. The HLO verifier already rejects original values whose tuple structure
differs from the instruction shape, so modules that pass verification are not
affected.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:LHS] Fix out-of-bounds access when no annotated node can be scheduled

head_commit.message:
[XLA:LHS] Fix out-of-bounds access when no annotated node can be scheduled

`FindAndExtractBestAnnotatedNode` removed the chosen node from the annotation
ready set by swapping it with the last element, without checking that a node
had been chosen. When every ready node of the annotation group crosses the
resource overlap limit, the iterator still points past the end of the vector,
so the swap read and wrote one element out of bounds before the caller reported
the failure.

Return early in that case and leave the ready set untouched. The caller already
turns the missing node into an error status, so scheduling such a module now
fails cleanly instead of corrupting memory.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Reject negative sort dimensions in the HLO verifier

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reject negative sort dimensions in the HLO verifier

`ShapeVerifier::HandleSort` only checked that the sort dimension is smaller
than the operand rank. Because the comparison is signed, a negative sort
dimension in an HLO module (for example one deserialized from a proto or
parsed from HLO text) passed verification. Passes and backend code
generation that run afterwards index operand shapes with the sort dimension
without further checks, which leads to out-of-bounds accesses.

The verifier now also requires the sort dimension to be non-negative, so
such modules are rejected with an error before any pass consumes them.

The error message now reports the rank of the first operand instead of
reading the dimensions of the sort result shape, which is a tuple for
sorts with more than one operand and cannot be queried for dimensions.

display_title: [ROCm] Fix ROCm multi-GPU CI failures.

head_commit.message:
[ROCm] Fix ROCm multi-GPU CI failures.

 - RcclCommunicator had no LaunchReduce; CollectiveReduce runtime support
   was added for NCCL only. Implemented on top of ncclReduce.
 - Backend::CreateGpuAllocators registered no collective memory space
   allocator, so any module whose device count equals the visible device
   count died with "No allocator found ... memory space 7" once buffer
   assignment colored its temp buffer S(7). Not ROCm specific.
 - MORI dlopen()s amd_smi by unversioned name and exit(-1)s when that
   fails, which no hermetic ROCm build can satisfy; XLA now hands it the
   path of the copy already mapped into the process.
 - ShardedAutotuningWorks hard-coded TCP port 12345 and failed when an
   unrelated process held it; it now picks a free port.
 - Symmetric-memory ragged-all-to-all needs a
   NCCL LSA window; it is CUDA-only and has no RCCL equivalent.
 - Command-buffer control flow and cross-host
   disabled on ROCm by CommandBufferConversionPass and IsLsaPossible().

name: CI
display_title: Bound the traversal of MLIR locations when exporting them to HLO metadata.

head_commit.message:
Bound the traversal of MLIR locations when exporting them to HLO metadata.

MLIR uniques locations, so nested locations (`CallSiteLoc`, `FusedLoc`,
`NameLoc`) can share sub-locations and form a DAG. The MHLO to HLO export
walked such locations recursively as trees when building op names, stack frames,
and source file/line metadata. With shared sub-locations, the work and the size
of the exported metadata grew exponentially with the nesting depth, and deeply
nested locations could overflow the C++ call stack.

Convert these traversals to iterative worklists, visit at most 4096 locations
per exported location, and cap the exported `op_name` at 4096 bytes by dropping
the names that do not fit. Locations emitted by frontends are far smaller, so
their metadata is unchanged; only pathologically nested or oversized locations
get truncated metadata. Empty names are now skipped instead of adding a
separator to the `op_name`.

Shared sub-locations are still visited every time they occur instead of being
deduplicated, because repeated locations are legitimate, for example the stack
frames of a recursive function.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] HostOffloader: do not follow tokens when walking host memory offload paths

head_commit.message:
[XLA] HostOffloader: do not follow tokens when walking host memory offload paths

📝 Summary of Changes

HostOffloader::WalkDownHostMemoryOffloadPaths follows the offloaded buffer through its users. For a generic user it keeps the same shape index, so a send user is tracked as the whole send result tuple, its send-done user is tracked as a token, and if that token is returned from the entry computation the pass ends up in the output streaming check, which does CHECK(leaf.has_layout()) on the entry result leaves. Tokens never have a layout, so the compiler aborts.

A token carries no data, so an offloaded buffer never flows through it (send-done only produces a token; the data stays in send's output {0}). This change skips token-shaped successors in the walk, and makes the output streaming check skip non-array leaves (the send result tuple itself has a token leaf, so returning the send from the entry computation hit the same CHECK). Arrays and tuples are handled exactly as before, and the existing send test (BasicHostTransferSendNoCrash) still gets its copy to host memory in front of the send.

🎯 Justification

Fixes #50971. The module from the issue (MoveToHost -> send -> send-done -> ROOT tuple(send-done)) aborts GPU compilation at HEAD with "Check failed: leaf.has_layout() Expecting output shape of entry computation to have a layout." With this change it gets the same clean error as the module without the MoveToHost ("Expected recv to match send", the fuzzer module has no matching recv), and a properly paired program compiles normally.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests:

Two new tests in xla/hlo/transforms/host_offloader_test.cc. SendDoneTokenReturnedFromEntryNoCrash runs the pass on the issue's module and checks that it succeeds, that the root is still tuple(send-done(send(copy(param), after-all))), that the copy is in host memory and the parameter is not, and that no annotations remain. SendResultReturnedFromEntryNoCrash returns the send itself from the entry computation and expects a clean error (the offloaded data would be returned in a device memory output). Without the source change both tests abort with the CHECK from the issue.

🧪 Execution Tests:

None added. Checked manually with run_hlo_module
