name: CI
display_title: PR #52161: [ROCm] Add a temp buffer pool for --xla_gpu_temp_buffer_use_separate_color

head_commit.message:
PR #52161: [ROCm] Add a temp buffer pool for --xla_gpu_temp_buffer_use_separate_color

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52161

ROCm only change, This is to help us get stable address which we can use to avoid collective recapture whenever stable address is there.

## 📝 Summary of Changes

On ROCm, `--xla_gpu_temp_buffer_use_separate_color` gets a separate, non-preallocated BFC pool per device for memory space `kTempBuffer`. Next to a preallocated default pool it may use the device memory that the default pool's memory fraction leaves, like the collective pool. without preallocation it has the default pool's limit.

## 🎯 Justification

The flag assigns temp buffers to `kTempBuffer`, but only CUDA registered an allocator for that space. On ROCm, an executable whose temp allocations are combined fails:

```
INTERNAL: No allocator found in MultiDeviceAdapter for device ordinal 0 and memory space 2
```

Only temp buffers use the new pool, so each execution gets the same temp address, which is what the flag is for.

- Like CUDA's pool, it sits outside the default pool: with a preallocated default pool, temp buffers must fit in what the default pool's memory fraction leaves, so a large temp buffer can run out of memory with the flag on and fit with it off. Lowering the memory fraction makes room, a fraction that leaves nothing is rejected when the client is created.
- Unlike CUDA's pool (sync mode), it does not synchronize the stream on allocate or free.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix · 🧪 Tests

## 🧪 Unit Tests

`se_gpu_pjrt_client_test`:
- `TempBufferColorUsesSeparatePool`: a `kTempBuffer` allocation leaves the default pool untouched and gets its address back after an intervening default allocation.
- `TempBufferColorKeepsTempAddressStable`: runs an HLO whose temp allocation is recoloured; checks the results and that the temp address stays the same over three executions.

Both fail without this change with the error above.

`gpu_helpers_test` (`BfcMemorySizingTest`):
- `TempBufferPoolGetsWhatAPreallocatedPoolLeaves`: next to a default pool preallocated at 0.75 of device memory, the temp pool's limit is the remaining quarter.
- `TempBufferPoolHasDefaultLimitWithoutPreallocation`: without preallocation the temp pool keeps the default pool's limit.
- `TempBufferPoolNeedsMemoryLeftByPreallocatedPool`: a fraction of 1.0 is rejected.

`allocator_config_test`: `MemFractionTest.LeftIsWhatTheStartFractionLeaves`.

These targets pass on MI355X (ROCm 10.2); `se_gpu_pjrt_client_test` and `gpu_helpers_test` also pass on B300 (CUDA 13).

## 🧪 Execution Tests

JAX on MI355X, ROCm 10.0, with the flag on 1 GPU and on 2 GPUs with an all-reduce: results are identical to the flag off under `--xla_gpu_deterministic_ops=true`.

Copybara import of the project:

--
ae99d2289ba86e86f86e697855400ce89855fe2d by magaonka <magaonka@amd.com>:

[ROCm] Add a temp buffer pool for --xla_gpu_temp_buffer_use_separate_color

- The flag puts temp buffers in memory space kTempBuffer, but only CUDA
  registered an allocator for it. On ROCm, execution failed with "No
  allocator found in MultiDeviceAdapter ... memory space 2".
- On ROCm, register a separate, non-preallocated BFC pool per device for
  kTempBuffer, named GPU_tempbuffer_<n>_bfc. Only temp buffers use it, so
  they keep the same address across executions.
- Next to a preallocated default pool, the temp pool gets the device
  memory that the default pool's start fraction leaves, like the
  collective pool; MemFractionLeft computes that remainder for both.
  Without preallocation it keeps the default pool's limit. Creating the
  client fails with a clear error if nothing is left for the temp pool.
- CreateBFCAllocator takes a name prefix (default "GPU", so existing
  pools keep GPU_<n>_bfc).
- In SharedPoolAnchorsCollectiveMemoryAtLowerEnd, convert device
  addresses to uintptr_t with reinterpret_cast instead of
  absl::bit_cast. The clang 18 static analyzer crashes comparing
  bit_cast pointer values, which fails clang-tidy on any change to
  this file.
- Update the flag's help text and add tests.

--
ee3abb0d3296b58da9517c0a1cd0b64f442a5480 by magaonka <magaonka@amd.com>:

[ROCm] Pass sub-allocator visitors to the temp buffer pool

- CreateTempBufferBFCAllocator takes the sub-allocator visitors, and the
  ROCm client passes the allocator config's, as for the default pool, so
  allocator memory registration also sees the temp pool's regions.
- Document at the call site and in the flag's help that next to a
  preallocated default pool without spatial partitioning, the separate
  collective pool gets the same limit as the temp pool and both take
  from the same remaining device memory.
- Test that the temp pool reports its regions to the visitors.

Merging this change closes #52161

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Move service/gpu/model to backends/gpu/cost_model

The GPU cost models (performance models, latency estimators, interpolators,
HLO op profiles) are a GPU backend component and belong under backends/gpu

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add CuDnnGemmDimensions to compute the dimensions of cuDNN GEMM fusions with ShapeTracker.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add CuDnnGemmDimensions to compute the dimensions of cuDNN GEMM fusions with ShapeTracker.

`CuDnnFusionCompiler` derives the sizes and strides of the tensors of dot /
scaled-dot cuDNN fusions with `TritonFusionAnalysis`, which is part of the
legacy Triton GEMM tiling infrastructure that we want to remove: it no longer
tiles or emits fusions and does not support many of today's fusions.

`CuDnnGemmDimensions` replaces it in a follow-up change (cl/1018233906), using these steps:

1.  Use ShapeTracker to relate every instruction to one 'port' of the dot (lhs, rhs, output).
2.  Check cuDNN restrictions (i.e. non-scalar instructions must relate to the dot in a single way, because the cuDNN graph has a single tensor per instruction - for example, `dot(p, p)` and `d + transpose(d)` are rejected).
3.  Use ShapeTracker to record sizes and strides of each operand and output. This translates all bitcasts/transposes that are allowed into sizes and strides for cuDNN to read the correct tensor for operand (e.g. [batch, M, K] for lhs).

I haven't replaced TritonFusionAnalysis immediately because I still need to support strides and split-M, which happen in follow up CLs.

display_title: [ROCm] Fix ROCm multi-GPU CI failures.

head_commit.message:
[ROCm] Fix ROCm multi-GPU CI failures.

 - RcclCommunicator had no LaunchReduce; CollectiveReduce runtime support
   was added for NCCL only. Implemented on top of ncclReduce.
 - Backend::CreateGpuAllocators registered no collective memory space
   allocator, so any module whose device count equals the visible device
   count died with "No allocator found ... memory space 7" once buffer
   assignment colored its temp buffer S(7). Not ROCm specific.
 - MORI dlopen()s amd_smi by unversioned name and exit(-1)s when that
   fails, which no hermetic ROCm build can satisfy; XLA now hands it the
   path of the copy already mapped into the process.
 - ShardedAutotuningWorks hard-coded TCP port 12345 and failed when an
   unrelated process held it; it now picks a free port.
 - Symmetric-memory ragged-all-to-all needs a
   NCCL LSA window; it is CUDA-only and has no RCCL equivalent.
 - Command-buffer control flow and cross-host
   disabled on ROCm by CommandBufferConversionPass and IsLsaPossible().

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Support slices in CuDnnGemmDimensions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Support slices in CuDnnGemmDimensions.

Slices are tracked alongside the ShapeTracker as per-dimension ranges of the
port of the dot: the ShapeTracker describes the unsliced tensor, and the ranges
become the `slices` of the cuDNN tensor. Nested slices are combined.

A slice can be followed by shape transformations before it reaches the dot,
e.g. `dot(transpose(slice(p)), ...)`. When a slice is reached, it is moved to
the port side of the ShapeTracker: the steps of the ShapeTracker are replayed
on the shape of the operand of the slice, carrying the sliced range of every
dimension along. Transposes permute the ranges. Reshapes can merge or split a
sliced dimension as long as the slice remains a range of a single dimension:
only the major-most dimension of a group of merged dimensions can be sliced,
and the range has to be aligned to the dimensions that it is split into.

A sliced dimension has to be a whole canonical dimension of the cuDNN tensor.
Strided slices are rejected. Slices of operands after the dot are rejected as
well: cuDNN builds plans for such graphs but fails to execute them
(CUDNN_STATUS_BAD_PARAM_NULL_POINTER).

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Work around large exportable VMM allocations on WSL

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Retry large exportable VMM allocations on WSL

WSL can reject large POSIX-FD VMM allocations with OUT_OF_MEMORY despite
sufficient free memory. Try the full-size allocation first, then retry
with backing chunks of at most 1 GiB on WSL with fabric handles disabled
and multicast unsupported. Exclude locality-domain allocations and map the
chunks into one contiguous virtual address range.

Keep POSIX-FD exportability to preserve multi-GPU support under WSL2.
Disabling enable_posix_fd_handle would be shorter, but removes handles
needed by cross-process GPU sharing and some NCCL paths.

Retain only the original first handle and release later creation
references after mapping. Track the mapped prefix for rollback and keep
the existing deallocation path.

Add a manual 6 GiB plus padding allocator regression and a WSL-only NCCL
regression that registers independent 6 GiB buffers, transfers the full
buffer, and checks both sides of each 1 GiB boundary. Skip the NCCL test
before GPU discovery on other operating systems and retain hardware,
memory, and chunking checks.

Validation: CUDA/NCCL builds, eight non-RDMA allocator tests, the manual
6 GiB regression, clang-format 17.0.6, and git diff --check pass. Three
upstream locality tests skip for version or hardware requirements. The
full two-GPU NCCL test skips on this single-GPU machine. Earlier local
two-process probes transferred a 6 GiB chunked source into an independent
256 MiB receiver; write and forced peer-read paths passed. The read probe
refreshed source registration per window and confirmed two-segment
imports at all five boundaries. Distinct-GPU execution remains untested.

display_title: Hoist stride-1 minor dimension out of BroadcastHelper inner loop in literal.cc.

head_commit.message:
Hoist stride-1 minor dimension out of BroadcastHelper inner loop in literal.cc.

BroadcastHelper previously invoked IndexUtil::MultidimensionalIndexToLinearIndex
and IndexUtil::BumpIndices on every output element, even along the contiguous
stride-1 most-minor layout dimension. Hoist result_minor_to_major[0] out of
broadcast_shape and fill inner_broadcast_size contiguous elements directly (via
memset for 1-byte elements and a contiguous memcpy loop otherwise), yielding a
1.52x geomean speedup across literal broadcast/populate benchmarks (14.24x on
BM_BroadcastVectorToMatrix/16/1024).

head_commit.message:
Emit GitHub Actions `::error` annotations from Bazel Build Event JSON (`--build_event_json_file`) when CI builds or tests fail, so failing target labels, invocation UUIDs / ResultStore or EngFlow URLs, and `test.log` tails are surfaced directly in the GitHub Check Runs Annotations API.

Changes:
- Add a concise `build_tools/ci/bep_annotations.py` (and `bep_annotations_test.py`) to parse failed/final-failed `testResult`, failed `action`, and `aborted` BEP events (skipping flaky tests that ultimately passed), extract the invocation ID / `--bes_results_url` link, and emit up to 10 bounded (`<= 3500` escaped chars) `::error` workflow commands per step with up to the last 50 lines of `test.log` / `stderr`. Always best-effort (never fails a job).
- Enable `--build_event_json_file=build_events.json` in `build_tools/ci/build.py` (`_DEFAULT_BAZEL_OPTIONS`), invoke `bep_annotations` on final Bazel failure or interrupt in GitHub Actions (covering `ci.yml` and `ci_multi_device.yml`), upload `build_events.json` in `ci.yml` failure artifacts, and update `golden_commands.txt` and `build_test.py`.
- Add best-effort (`continue-on-error: true`, `if: failure() || cancelled()`) annotation steps to `.github/workflows/rocm_ci.yml` for both the JAX and XLA jobs.

name: CI
display_title: Cache XLA LocalClient instances by allowed_devices

head_commit.message:
Cache XLA LocalClient instances by allowed_devices

`ClientLibrary::GetOrCreateLocalClient` previously keyed `local_instances_` only on `platform->id()`, ignoring `options.allowed_devices()` on cache hits. When multiple `PjRtClient` instances (or TensorFlow and PJRT clients) were created in the same process with different `allowed_devices` sets, every call after the first received the first call's `LocalClient` and its `StreamExecutor` list.

Therefore this change keys `ClientLibrary::local_instances_` by `(platform->id(), options.allowed_devices())` so each `allowed_devices` configuration gets a `LocalClient` restricted to those devices, while `DestroyLocalInstance(platform)` still clears all cached instances for that platform. It also:
- Updates `PjRtStreamExecutorRawClient::UpdateCompileOptions` to fall back to `client()->default_device_ordinal()` instead of hardcoding device ordinal `0`, which fails when `allowed_devices` does not include device `0`.
- Forwards `visible_devices` in `GetTargetConfigFromOptions` (`xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_gpu_internal.cc`) when creating a GPU topology description via the PJRT C API.
- Preserves `allowed_devices` in `XlaDevice::Metadata` when looking up the `LocalClient`.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Don't annotate integer abs as non-negative if the input may be INT_MIN

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Don't annotate integer abs as non-negative if the input may be INT_MIN

`SimplifyArithPass` annotated the result of the integer abs pattern
`select(x >= 0, x, 0 - x)` with the range `[0, INT_MAX]` even if nothing was
known about `x`. This does not hold for the minimum signed value, for which
`0 - x` wraps around to `x` itself, so the result is negative. The unsound
range could then be used to drop a lower-bound clamp on an index computed from
such a value.

Only annotate the result if the range of `x` is known and excludes the minimum
signed value of its type. The annotation for inputs whose known range excludes
that value is unchanged.

To keep the clamp of such an index cheap, rewrite
`maxsi(minsi(index_cast(|x|), C), 0)` to `minui(index_castui(|x|), C)`.
Interpreted as an unsigned value, `|x|` of the minimum signed value is larger
than `C`, so one unsigned comparison clamps `|x|` for all values of `x`. An
index of the minimum signed value is now clamped to the upper bound instead of
to 0.

Add execution tests for gather and dynamic-slice with 32 and 64 bit start
indices that are the abs of the minimum signed value.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1020985486

display_title: [XLA:Interpreter] Run the HLO verifier in the PJRT interpreter

head_commit.message:
[XLA:Interpreter] Run the HLO verifier in the PJRT interpreter

The PJRT interpreter created an `HloModule` from a proto and then ran its pass
pipeline and `DynamicDimensionInference` on it without running the HLO
verifier, both when compiling a computation and when deserializing an
executable. Code on these paths relies on invariants that only the verifier
enforces. For example, dynamic dimension inference indexes into the result
shape of a reshape with its `inferred_dimension`, so an out-of-range value led
to out-of-bounds accesses.

Run `HloVerifier` right after the module is created in both entry points, so
that an invalid module is rejected with an error before anything else consumes
it.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1020982563

display_title: PR #52971: [AlgebraicSimplifier] Gate constant reciprocal division rewrite on fast math

head_commit.message:
PR #52971: [AlgebraicSimplifier] Gate constant reciprocal division rewrite on fast math

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52971

#ai-generated

Fixes #52968.

## Status quo

`HandleDivide` rewrites floating-point division by a constant into multiplication by a rounded reciprocal, including when `enable_fast_math` is false.

## Why

We encountered this while comparing an ONNX quantized MLP across execution backends. For float32 `[-100, 0.1, 100]`, the scale `200 / 255` changes by one ULP. The subsequent zero-point calculation crosses a rounding boundary, producing 127 instead of 128. The issue includes an independent JAX reproduction with CPU fast math disabled.

## Design choices

Require `enable_fast_math` for this rewrite. Add scalar and broadcasted-constant tests with fast math disabled, and explicitly enable fast math in the existing reciprocal-rewrite tests.

## Trade-offs

This retains the rewrite in fast-math mode. With fast math disabled, it preserves division and may reduce strength-reduction opportunities. Performance impact has not been benchmarked.

## Testing

The two new regression tests fail against the original implementation. With the fix, all 2,069 tests in `algebraic_simplifier_test` pass locally using Bazel 8.8.2 and Clang 21 on Linux x86-64.

The broader `bazel test //xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers/...` run also passes all 50 test targets.

display_title: [XLA] Add ShapeTracker::TryGetStridedView().

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Add ShapeTracker::TryGetStridedView().

`TryGetStridedView()` returns, for every output dimension of the tracker, the
segments (strides and extents) of the input that the dimension iterates over.
Broadcasted segments have stride 0, and a dimension can span several segments,
e.g. when a reshape merges two dimensions that were transposed apart. It
returns std::nullopt if the tracked transformation is not a strided view of the
input, i.e. if materializing it would require a copy or a reduction.

This will be used to compute the sizes and strides of the tensors of cuDNN GEMM
fusions (see cl/1017387793).

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Don't annotate integer abs as non-negative if the input may be INT_MIN

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Don't annotate integer abs as non-negative if the input may be INT_MIN

`SimplifyArithPass` annotated the result of the integer abs pattern
`select(x >= 0, x, 0 - x)` with the range `[0, INT_MAX]` even if nothing was
known about `x`. This does not hold for the minimum signed value, for which
`0 - x` wraps around to `x` itself, so the result is negative. The unsound
range could then be used to drop a lower-bound clamp on an index computed from
such a value.

Only annotate the result if the range of `x` is known and excludes the minimum
signed value of its type. The annotation for inputs whose known range excludes
that value is unchanged.

To keep the clamp of such an index cheap, rewrite
`maxsi(minsi(index_cast(|x|), C), 0)` to `minui(index_castui(|x|), C)`.
Interpreted as an unsigned value, `|x|` of the minimum signed value is larger
than `C`, so one unsigned comparison clamps `|x|` for all values of `x`. An
index of the minimum signed value is now clamped to the upper bound instead of
to 0.

Add execution tests for gather and dynamic-slice with 32 and 64 bit start
indices that are the abs of the minimum signed value.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019017906

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Validate in-place collective-permute protos during deserialization

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Validate in-place collective-permute protos during deserialization

`HloInstruction::CreateFromProto` regroups the flat `dynamic_slice_sizes` of an
in-place `collective-permute` or `collective-permute-start` into one list per
slice, based on the shapes of the input and start-indices operands. Those
operands and shapes come from the proto and have not been verified at that
point, yet they were used without validation. A proto with fewer than four
operands, with start indices that are not (nested) non-empty tuples, or with
fewer slice sizes than the shapes imply caused out-of-bounds reads, and start
indices describing more slices for a later buffer than for the first one caused
an out-of-bounds write. The existing `CHECK_GE` bound on `dynamic_slice_sizes`
was also off by one.

Return an error for such protos instead: require exactly four operands, check
the operand shapes before indexing into them, require start indices for every
buffer with the same number of slices each, and require `dynamic_slice_sizes`
to hold exactly as many entries as those shapes imply.

These checks cannot live only in the HLO verifier: the invalid accesses happen
while the instruction is being constructed, before a verifier can run, and the
verifier never sees the flat `dynamic_slice_sizes` field.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1020952944

name: CI
display_title: Guard RawBufferEntry and PjRtBufferEntry state against concurrent Handle calls.

head_commit.message:
Guard RawBufferEntry and PjRtBufferEntry state against concurrent Handle calls.

`PullTable::Handle` releases the table lock before calling `Entry::Handle`, and
`AwaitPull` replays paused pulls on the registering thread after the entry has
been published. A pull that arrives on the event loop thread at that moment runs
`Entry::Handle` concurrently on the same entry. `RawBufferEntry` and
`PjRtBufferEntry` moved the buffer out of their per-buffer state and updated
`num_consumed_bufs_` without synchronization (`mu_` was declared but never
acquired), so two threads could both take ownership of the same buffer
reference, corrupting its reference count and leading to a use-after-free.

Both entries now take the buffer out of `arrs_` and update `num_consumed_bufs_`

display_title: [XLA] Validate reshape inferred_dimension in the HLO verifier

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Validate reshape inferred_dimension in the HLO verifier

`ShapeVerifier::HandleReshape` only checked element types and element counts and
did not validate `inferred_dimension`. Dynamic dimension inference later uses
`inferred_dimension` to index into the dimensions of the result shape and into a
vector with one entry per result dimension, so a value outside `[-1, rank)` led
to out-of-bounds accesses.

Check in `ShapeVerifier::HandleReshape` that `inferred_dimension` is either -1
(unset) or a valid dimension index of the result shape. The handler now also
requires the operand and result shapes to be arrays, which the rank lookup
relies on. Validating the invariant in the HLO verifier covers every path that
verifies the module, including reshapes rewritten by compiler passes. The PJRT
interpreter does not run the verifier yet; a follow-up change adds it there.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Only fold max(a, clamp(a, x, b)) into the clamp when a <= b

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Only fold max(a, clamp(a, x, b)) into the clamp when a <= b

📝 Summary of Changes

AlgebraicSimplifier rewrites maximum(a, clamp(a, x, b)) to clamp(a, x, b). That is only right when a <= b: with a > b the clamp is b for every x (clamp is min(max(a, x), b)) while the maximum is a. Nothing in XLA or StableHLO requires the clamp bounds to be ordered, so the rewrite silently changes results when they are not.

This change makes HandleMaximum apply the fold only when both clamp bounds are effective-scalar constants (or broadcasts of them) of the same element type that compare as lower <= upper. Programs with runtime bounds keep the extra maximum; programs with ordered constant bounds are folded as before. The compare is done with HloEvaluator, the same way MinMaxToClamp already checks lower < upper for max(lo, min(x, hi)); that check is factored into a small shared helper so both rules use the same code. With runtime bounds or inverted constants the maximum is left alone. Dropping the rule entirely would also fix the issue; I kept it with the guard since the constant-bounds case is the common one, happy to remove it instead if preferred.

🎯 Justification

Fixes #52659. jax.jit(lambda a, b, c: lax.max(a, lax.clamp(a, b, c))) returns 0 instead of 10 for (10, 5, 0) on CPU and GPU at head; correct with --xla_disable_hlo_passes=algsimp. After this change run_hlo_module --platform=CUDA --reference_platform=interpreter agrees on the three-parameter module in 8/8 runs (1/8 mismatched before).

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests:

xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers/algebraic_simplifier_test.cc:
- MaxOfClamp now uses ordered constant bounds (0 and 6) and still expects the fold.
- MaxOfClampWithBroadcastBounds: same with broadcast bounds on an array, and the maximum operands swapped; expects the fold.
- MaxOfClampWithUnorderedBounds: constant bounds 10 and 0, maximum operands in the other order; expects no change. Fails without the fix.
- MaxOfClampWithParameterBounds: the issue's module with parameter bounds; expects no change. Fails without the fix.

🧪 Execution Tests:

None added; checked by hand with run_hlo_module against the interpreter

display_title: PR #52971: [AlgebraicSimplifier] Gate constant reciprocal division rewrite on fast math

head_commit.message:
PR #52971: [AlgebraicSimplifier] Gate constant reciprocal division rewrite on fast math

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52971

#ai-generated

Fixes #52968.

## Status quo

`HandleDivide` rewrites floating-point division by a constant into multiplication by a rounded reciprocal, including when `enable_fast_math` is false.

## Why

We encountered this while comparing an ONNX quantized MLP across execution backends. For float32 `[-100, 0.1, 100]`, the scale `200 / 255` changes by one ULP. The subsequent zero-point calculation crosses a rounding boundary, producing 127 instead of 128. The issue includes an independent JAX reproduction with CPU fast math disabled.

## Design choices

Require `enable_fast_math` for this rewrite. Add scalar and broadcasted-constant tests with fast math disabled, and explicitly enable fast math in the existing reciprocal-rewrite tests.

## Trade-offs

This retains the rewrite in fast-math mode. With fast math disabled, it preserves division and may reduce strength-reduction opportunities. Performance impact has not been benchmarked.

## Testing

The two new regression tests fail against the original implementation. With the fix, all 2,069 tests in `algebraic_simplifier_test` pass locally using Bazel 8.8.2 and Clang 21 on Linux x86-64.

The broader `bazel test //xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers/...` run also passes all 50 test targets.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Validate in-place collective-permute protos during deserialization

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Validate in-place collective-permute protos during deserialization

`HloInstruction::CreateFromProto` regroups the flat `dynamic_slice_sizes` of an
in-place `collective-permute` or `collective-permute-start` into one list per
slice, based on the shapes of the input and start-indices operands. Those
operands and shapes come from the proto and have not been verified at that
point, yet they were used without validation. A proto with fewer than four
operands, with start indices that are not (nested) non-empty tuples, or with
fewer slice sizes than the shapes imply caused out-of-bounds reads, and start
indices describing more slices for a later buffer than for the first one caused
an out-of-bounds write. The existing `CHECK_GE` bound on `dynamic_slice_sizes`
was also off by one.

Return an error for such protos instead: require exactly four operands, check
the operand shapes before indexing into them, require start indices for every
buffer with the same number of slices each, and require `dynamic_slice_sizes`
to hold exactly as many entries as those shapes imply.

These checks cannot live only in the HLO verifier: the invalid accesses happen
while the instruction is being constructed, before a verifier can run, and the
verifier never sees the flat `dynamic_slice_sizes` field.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019018379

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Use named barrier 1 for single-block phase transitions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Use named barrier 1 for single-block phase transitions.

This prevents `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION` errors when generalizing MultiStageFusion to column reduction and transpose that emit block barriers themselves.

In `ThreadBlockSpecializedFusion`, consecutive single-block phases synchronize via `bar.sync 0` across all `max_threads` of block 0, while partial-CTA sub-kernels (`sub_threads < max_threads`) rewrite intra-phase barriers to `barrier.sync 0, sub_threads` on the same hardware barrier 0. When a partial-CTA reduction or transpose runs as a single-block phase followed by another single-block phase, threads with `tid >= sub_threads` skip the sub-kernel and reach the trailing `bar.sync 0`, arming barrier 0 with thread count `max_threads` while active threads arrive at barrier 0 with thread count `sub_threads`, raising `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1020935404

head_commit.message:
[XLA:Interpreter] Run the HLO verifier in the PJRT interpreter

The PJRT interpreter created an `HloModule` from a proto and then ran its pass
pipeline and `DynamicDimensionInference` on it without running the HLO
verifier, both when compiling a computation and when deserializing an
executable. Code on these paths relies on invariants that only the verifier
enforces. For example, dynamic dimension inference indexes into the result
shape of a reshape with its `inferred_dimension`, so an out-of-range value led
to out-of-bounds accesses.

Run `HloVerifier` right after the module is created in both entry points, so
that an invalid module is rejected with an error before anything else consumes
it.

name: CI
display_title: Make the async events ids of host execute thunks deterministic

head_commit.message:
Make the async events ids of host execute thunks deterministic

HostExecuteStartThunk and HostExecuteDoneThunk serialized
`async_events_unique_id` as the address of the `HostExecuteAsyncEvents` object
they share, so a serialized GPU executable differed on every compilation, and
AOT golden comparisons could not compare the id. AsyncStartThunk and
AsyncDoneThunk already use the start thunk's ThunkId for the same purpose.

Store the id in `HostExecuteAsyncEvents`, seeded from `HostExecuteStartThunk`'s
`ThunkId`. `FromProto` preserves the serialized id so start/done pairing works
in either deserialization order and round-trips keep the original id, including
address-based ids written by older runtimes.

The proto schema does not change, and `FromProto` only uses the id to pair
thunks, so executables serialized by older and newer runtimes stay loadable in
both directions.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019965378

name: CI
display_title: Clean up host send/recv thunks.

head_commit.message:
Clean up host send/recv thunks.

1: Stop emitting async_events_unique_id: it used to serialize the address of the shared  `HostSendRecvAsyncEvents`, which makes serialized  GPUExecutables non-determenistic.

Looking closer, I saw that async_unique_id is redundant -- an executable has a single `HostSendRecvAsyncEvents` shared by all host send/recv thunks, events keyed by device and channel id. So I stop populating `async_events_unique_id` in `ToProto` and delete (and reserve) the proto field.

----

2: Delete HostAsyncThunk. There are no users of the shared methods, so I'm removing unnessecary level of abstraction and inherit from Thunk class directly. IsAsyncStart/IsAsyncDone methods were initially added to support folding async thunks into command buffers. HostSendRecv[Done]Thunk can not be added to command buffer, so this are leftover bits

----

This doesn't break compatibility
* Backwards: the old executable has the field set to some address. The new runtime ignores it and all send/recv thunks still share one object
* Forwards: the field is missing, so the old runtime reads 0. It groups every send/recv thunk under key 0, which also gives one shared object.

host_async_thunk.h goes away in the following cl.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1020841895

name: CI
display_title: PR #46248: Fix collective-permute cycle decomposer for multiple cycles

head_commit.message:
PR #46248: Fix collective-permute cycle decomposer for multiple cycles

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46248

`DecomposeCollectivePermuteCycle` recombines the backward and forward collective-permutes using a `select` predicate that previously compared the partition or replica ID only against `back_pairs.back().second` (the last back-edge target). When `source_target_pairs` contains multiple disjoint cycles, `GetCycleTypeAndIndices` breaks out one back edge per cycle into `back_pairs`, so every back-edge receiver except the last routed through the forward collective-permute (where it is not a target) and read zeros instead of its permuted data.

Compare the partition or replica ID against every target in `back_pairs` and combine the equality predicates with `or` so all back-edge receivers select the backward collective-permute, leaving single-cycle HLO output unchanged. Also incorporates review feedback from #46248 (updating the header pseudocode comment and adding multi-cycle backward coverage in `CollectivePermuteCycleDecomposerTest`).

Fixes #45222

Merging this change closes #46248

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Rename general, debugging, and Triton autotuner flags.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Rename general, debugging, and Triton autotuner flags.

Several autotuner flags carry legacy `gpu` or `gemm` prefixes even though they
apply to config assignment across backends or specifically target Triton
configs. Rename them to clearer, accurately scoped names:

- `--xla_gpu_experimental_autotune_backends` → `--xla_config_assigner_backends`
- `--xla_gpu_autotune_gemm_rtol` → `--xla_autotune_rtol`
- `--xla_gpu_dump_autotuned_instructions` →
  `--xla_dump_isolated_hlos_pre_and_post_config_assignment`
- `--xla_gpu_dump_autotune_logs_to` → `--xla_dump_autotune_logs_to`
- `--xla_gpu_override_gemm_autotuner` → `--xla_gpu_override_triton_config`
- `--xla_gpu_gemm_autotuner_override_file` →
  `--xla_gpu_override_triton_configs_file`

Add the new fields to `DebugOptions`, remove and reserve the old proto fields in
`xla.proto`, and keep the deprecated CLI flags as aliases that populate the new
proto fields for backward compatibility.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1020888276

display_title: PR #52528: [XLA] Skip implicit broadcast rewrite for zero-bound dynamic dims

head_commit.message:
PR #52528: [XLA] Skip implicit broadcast rewrite for zero-bound dynamic dims

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52528

Fixes #49925.

`RewriteDynamicBinaryOp` slices a size-1 window along a dynamic dimension to
insert an implicit broadcast, assuming the dimension's static bound is at least
1. When the bound is 0 the dimension is always empty: both operands have size
0, so there is nothing to broadcast. The rewrite runs anyway and emits

  slice(%a), slice={[0:1], [0:2]}   // %a: f32[0,2]

which the verifier rejects with "limit index (1) must be less than or equal to
dimension size (0)".

This shows up from TF via `tf.math.is_non_decreasing` on a tensor with a
dynamic dim: the comparison ends up in a `tf.cond` branch whose operands have a
`<=0` bound.

Skip the rewrite when the bound is 0 and add a regression test.

`bazel test //xla/service:dynamic_padder_test_cpu`

Copybara import of the project:

--
d0ece8f28acd750f5939d6cec04b52fc047eda95 by Iris <244965872+BlueIrisSky@users.noreply.github.com>:

[XLA] Fix out-of-bounds slice in DynamicPadder implicit broadcast rewrite

RewriteDynamicBinaryOp inserts an implicit broadcast when the operands of an
elementwise binary op have a dynamic dimension with different runtime sizes.
The rewrite extracts a size-1 slice along the dimension, reshapes the
dimension away and broadcasts the result back to the full shape.

When the dimension's static bound is zero the dimension is always empty: both
dynamic sizes are necessarily zero, so no implicit broadcast can ever be
needed. The rewrite nevertheless ran and emitted an out-of-bounds slice,

  slice(%a), slice={[0:1], [0:2]}   // %a: f32[0,2]

which fails HLO verification with

  limit index (1) must be less than or equal to dimension size (0)

This is reachable from TF through tf.math.is_non_decreasing and
tf.math.is_strictly_increasing, which wrap the comparison in a tf.cond whose
branch operands end up with a zero bound:
https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/49925

Skip the rewrite when the static bound of the dimension is zero and add a
regression test.

--
48493ecb10c5cd71598755e8cf7c7f199f9bd3b2 by Iris <244965872+BlueIrisSky@users.noreply.github.com>:

[XLA] Add HLO IR check for zero-bound dynamic binary op test

Address review feedback by adding a DynamicPadderTest unit test that runs
DynamicPadder directly and verifies no slice/select/reshape rewrite is
emitted for zero-bound dynamic compare operands.

Merging this change closes #52528

display_title: PR #52821: [XLA:GPU] Run stream-annotated computations on locality domains

head_commit.message:
PR #52821: [XLA:GPU] Run stream-annotated computations on locality domains

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52821

📝 Summary of Changes

Lets an XLA program run a computation on a chosen locality domain by annotating a call with `_xla_stream_annotation="locality_domain:<id>"`. Builds on the stream building blocks ([#52124](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52124)) and their execution support ([#52246](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52302)).
- `ExplicitStreamAnnotationAsyncWrapper`: wraps a locality-domain-annotated call into an async region. It rejects regions that contain collectives, send/recv or nested stream annotations, and annotations that aren't on a non-inlineable call.
- `ExecutionStreamAssignment`: assigns `LocalityDomainStreamId(<id>)` to those regions, without using up a round-robin compute stream.
- `AsyncStartThunk::Prepare`: rejects communication thunks inside a locality-domain region at runtime.
- **MHLO → HLO**: stream annotations stay on the call, not on the get-tuple-elements that unpack a multi-result call.
- `side_effect_util`: adds `kXlaLocalityDomainStreamAnnotationPrefix` (`"locality_domain:"`).

🎯 Justification

This is the first PR that lets a program annotate calls to run on a locality domain's stream, using the runtime support from [#52246](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52302). Programs without these annotations are unchanged.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

N/A: this enables locality-domain execution

🧪 Unit Tests:

- `ExecutionStreamAssignmentTest`:
  - `ValidLocalityDomainAnnotationTest.AssignsLocalityDomainStream`;
  - `MalformedLocalityDomainAnnotationTest.DiesWithCheckMessage`;
  - `LocalityDomainAnnotationRejectsCommunicationScope`;
  - `LocalityDomainDoesNotConsumeRoundRobinStream`.
- `ExplicitStreamAnnotationAsyncWrapperTest` (10 tests):
  - wrapping a call while keeping its attributes; idempotence; tuple calls with get-tuple-element users;
  - rejecting missing or inlineable calls, transitive collectives, nested annotations and send/recv;
  - returning an error status inside fusions and async computations.
- `AsyncThunkTest.LocalityDomainPrepareRejectsCommunicationThunks`: a compute-only region prepares successfully, and one containing a communication thunk is rejected.
- `frontend_attributes.mlir`: stream annotations aren't copied onto the get-tuple-elements of a multi-result call.

🧪 Execution Tests:

display_title: PR #46248: Fix collective-permute cycle decomposer for multiple cycles

head_commit.message:
PR #46248: Fix collective-permute cycle decomposer for multiple cycles

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46248

`DecomposeCollectivePermuteCycle` recombines the backward and forward collective-permutes using a `select` predicate that previously compared the partition or replica ID only against `back_pairs.back().second` (the last back-edge target). When `source_target_pairs` contains multiple disjoint cycles, `GetCycleTypeAndIndices` breaks out one back edge per cycle into `back_pairs`, so every back-edge receiver except the last routed through the forward collective-permute (where it is not a target) and read zeros instead of its permuted data.

Compare the partition or replica ID against every target in `back_pairs` and combine the equality predicates with `or` so all back-edge receivers select the backward collective-permute, leaving single-cycle HLO output unchanged. Also incorporates review feedback from #46248 (updating the header pseudocode comment and adding multi-cycle backward coverage in `CollectivePermuteCycleDecomposerTest`).

Fixes #45222

Merging this change closes #46248

display_title: PR #52201: [XLA:GPU][Triton] Fix collective while-loop command buffer tests on ROCm

head_commit.message:
PR #52201: [XLA:GPU][Triton] Fix collective while-loop command buffer tests on ROCm

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52201

📝 Summary of Changes
On ROCm, where HIP graphs have no conditional nodes: CommandBufferConversionPass drops the WHILE command and captures the loop body into a command buffer nested inside the WhileThunk. The 20-collective while-loop tests for all-gather, all-reduce and all-to-all additionally asserted that the kWhile thunk itself is captured, which only holds on CUDA, so those two expectations are now guarded by Capability().IsCuda().

`CountThunksInDump` only tracked command buffer membership for top-level thunks, so thunks inside a nested kCommandBuffer were counted as being outside one. Track the indentation of the innermost enclosing kCommandBuffer instead.

🎯 Justification
On ROCm, the `Twenty*InWhileLoopWithCudaGraphs` multi-gpu single host triton collective op tests (`all_gather_e2e_test`, `all_reduce_e2e_test`, `all_to_all_e2e_test`) fail because HIP graphs have no conditional nodes.
These tests must therefore be adapted so that they pass on both Cuda and ROCm.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

display_title: PR #52875: [XLA:CPU] Prevent unsafe buffer reuse in oneDNN fusions

head_commit.message:
PR #52875: [XLA:CPU] Prevent unsafe buffer reuse in oneDNN fusions

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52875

A fused FP32 matmul followed by `maximum(product, zeros)` can return negative values on the oneDNN/ACL path. XLA permits the output to reuse the zero operand's buffer, but matmul overwrites those zeros before maximum reads them. The regression returns `[[6, -6], [-12, 12]]` without the fix instead of `[[6, 0], [0, 12]]`.

Use a shared CPU alias policy during copy insertion, scheduling, buffer assignment and AOT loading. Custom fusions deny inferred input/output reuse by default; YNNPACK retains the usual HLO shape/use checks. oneDNN's compiled partition requirements are unavailable during compilation. Fusion remains enabled, with potentially higher buffer memory use and protective copies for aliased inputs. Saved executable formats and existing allocations are unchanged.

Validation:

- 39 focused test executions pass across AArch64 QEMU N1, SVE256 and SVE512: allocation rules, internal and aliased zero inputs, YNNPACK reuse, and AOT export/load.
- Removing only the copy-insertion policy makes both new aliased-input regressions fail while the original internal-broadcast regression still passes.
- The original 17x23 by 23x19 reproducer passes six numerical comparisons across those profiles, still using `gemm:acl` with the fused maximum.
- Clang-format 17.0.6, buildifier 6.4.0 and whitespace checks pass.

A previous broader sweep found an unrelated SVE512 batched-matmul mismatch using oneDNN's `brg:sve_512`. It predates this change and remains unresolved. These are correctness tests under emulation, not native performance measurements.

Copybara import of the project:

--
31a033f4fa91d10341fdf72912cb598e76a438e7 by Pablo Marquez Tello <pablo.tello@arm.com>:

[XLA:CPU] Prevent unsafe buffer reuse in oneDNN fusions

Keep oneDNN fusion outputs separate from their inputs because the
compiled partition's in-place requirements are unavailable during
buffer assignment. This prevents fused matmul from overwriting the
zero operand before maximum applies ReLU.

Add allocation and execution regressions while preserving buffer reuse
for ordinary loop fusions.

Signed-off-by: Pablo Marquez Tello <pablo.tello@arm.com>

--
a5ff64ae155c8f93a879135eefae6eaff7bb042a by Pablo Marquez Tello <pablo.tello@arm.com>:

[XLA:CPU] Preserve safe custom fusion buffer reuse

Deny inferred buffer reuse for custom fusions unless their runtime
supports it. Preserve YNNPACK's existing HLO sharing rules and share
CpuAliasInfo between compilation and AOT loading.

Cover aliased oneDNN inputs through copy insertion and execution, plus
YNNPACK reuse. Keep the regression enabled on AArch64.

Signed-off-by: Pablo Marquez Tello <pablo.tello@arm.com>

[XLA:CPU] Fix fusion test CI checks

Add the headers and Bazel dependencies used by the fusion regressions.
Teach DWYU to recognize dependencies inside if_onednn, and cover the

display_title: PR #52604: [XLA:GPU] Refresh the B300 target spec from a live B300

head_commit.message:
PR #52604: [XLA:GPU] Refresh the B300 target spec from a live B300

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52604

#ai-generated

Fixes #52602

### Status quo
`b300.txtpb` (from #34116, source device not stated) has 158 SMs, a 1.965 GHz clock, 297021865984 B of memory, 7.936 TB/s and a 135528448 B L2. A live B300 SXM6 AC reports 148, 2.032 GHz, 287416123392 B, 7.672 TB/s and 132644864 B. The spec also has no `name`, so `SpecMatchesLiveDevice` skips on B300, and it lacks the fields that the refreshed b200/gb300 specs carry.

### Why
Deviceless/AOT compiles for `GpuModel.B300` should see the same device as an on-device compile. With the current spec, for example, a bf16 elementwise kernel gets 128-bit vectors deviceless and 256-bit on device (65536 vs 32768 blocks for 2^26 elements).

### Design
- Regenerated from the `gpu_target_config.pbtxt` that `--xla_dump_to` writes on a B300 (jaxlib 0.12.1.dev20261108).
- Dropped the per-host fields `numa_node`, `pci_bus_id`, `kernel_mode_driver_version` and the top-level `runtime_version`. Of the checked-in specs, only vr_nvl72.txtpb has them.
- Kept `driver_version: "13.0.0"`, as in gb200/gb300/h100_sxm. `SupportsMovedChildCommands` reads it, so leaving it unset would turn moved child commands off for deviceless compiles.
- Kept `device_description_str: "NVIDIA B300"`, since `gpu_topology.cc` maps "NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC" to it.
- `name` is the live `NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC`.
- Version fields follow b200.txtpb: runtime/toolkit 13.2.0, cuDNN 9.23.0, CUB 3.1.2. The live machine had pip CUDA 13.5 and cuDNN 9.28.1, which describe the test environment rather than the device.
- Data only, no code change. #52432 adds memory bus width to other specs and does not touch this file; whichever lands second can add it here.

### Tests
- A deviceless JAX compile against the new spec gives the same `loop_add_fusion` launch (32768 x 128) as the live B300 does; the old spec gives 65536 x 128.
- The spec parses: deviceless compiles with it succeed.
- If the current values describe another B300 SKU, this should become a separate spec rather than a replacement (question in #52602).
- Not run: `CudnnDevicePropsTest.SpecMatchesLiveDevice` on B300 (needs a `--config=cuda` build). Only one B300 SKU (SXM6 AC) was available, so other B300 SKUs may report different values.

It also lacks the fields the other refreshed Blackwell specs carry. Regenerate it from the gpu_target_config dumped on a B300, keeping device_description_str and using the same runtime/toolkit/cuDNN/CUB version convention as b200.txtpb.

[XLA:GPU] Keep driver_version in the B300 target spec

SupportsMovedChildCommands in command_buffer_conversion_pass.cc takes the
minimum of the runtime, driver and toolkit versions, so an unset
driver_version turns moved child commands off for deviceless compiles.
Restore the previous 13.0.0, which gb200, gb300 and h100_sxm also use.

Signed-off-by: 0z5a <dezhen.lu@student.uni-tuebingen.de>

Merging this change closes #52604

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Rename general, debugging, and Triton autotuner flags.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Rename general, debugging, and Triton autotuner flags.

Several autotuner flags carry legacy `gpu` or `gemm` prefixes even though they
apply to config assignment across backends or specifically target Triton
configs. Rename them to clearer, accurately scoped names:

- `--xla_gpu_experimental_autotune_backends` → `--xla_config_assigner_backends`
- `--xla_gpu_autotune_gemm_rtol` → `--xla_autotune_rtol`
- `--xla_gpu_dump_autotuned_instructions` →
  `--xla_dump_isolated_hlos_pre_and_post_config_assignment`
- `--xla_gpu_dump_autotune_logs_to` → `--xla_dump_autotune_logs_to`
- `--xla_gpu_override_gemm_autotuner` → `--xla_gpu_override_triton_config`
- `--xla_gpu_gemm_autotuner_override_file` →
  `--xla_gpu_override_triton_configs_file`

Add the new fields to `DebugOptions`, remove and reserve the old proto fields in
`xla.proto`, and keep the deprecated CLI flags as aliases that populate the new
proto fields for backward compatibility.

display_title: PR #52201: [XLA:GPU][Triton] Fix collective while-loop command buffer tests on ROCm

head_commit.message:
PR #52201: [XLA:GPU][Triton] Fix collective while-loop command buffer tests on ROCm

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52201

📝 Summary of Changes
On ROCm, where HIP graphs have no conditional nodes: CommandBufferConversionPass drops the WHILE command and captures the loop body into a command buffer nested inside the WhileThunk. The 20-collective while-loop tests for all-gather, all-reduce and all-to-all additionally asserted that the kWhile thunk itself is captured, which only holds on CUDA, so those two expectations are now guarded by Capability().IsCuda().

`CountThunksInDump` only tracked command buffer membership for top-level thunks, so thunks inside a nested kCommandBuffer were counted as being outside one. Track the indentation of the innermost enclosing kCommandBuffer instead.

🎯 Justification
On ROCm, the `Twenty*InWhileLoopWithCudaGraphs` multi-gpu single host triton collective op tests (`all_gather_e2e_test`, `all_reduce_e2e_test`, `all_to_all_e2e_test`) fail because HIP graphs have no conditional nodes.
These tests must therefore be adapted so that they pass on both Cuda and ROCm.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
Please remove what does not apply: 🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

head_commit.message:
[ROCm] Gate collectives out of output allocations behind a flag

- Add xla_gpu_command_buffer_keep_collectives_out_of_outputs (default
  false). CreateMustNotLiveOut installs the predicate only when it is set.
- Do not match host send/recv: they lower to host send/recv thunks, which
  are never recorded.
- gpu_compiler_test checks maybe_live_out of the all-reduce's allocation
  instead of comparing temp allocation sizes.

display_title: PR #52104: [ROCm] [CUDA] Keep recorded collectives out of output allocations under VA remapping

head_commit.message:
PR #52104: [ROCm] [CUDA] Keep recorded collectives out of output allocations under VA remapping Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52104 Shared GPU code (CUDA and ROCm). This is mainly beneficial to ROCm, where re-recording a collective on every execution is costly. from CUDA side change is not regressive but not greatly beneficial either (Tested on B300). from ROCm side I'm trying find ways to reduce the recapture whenever possible this is one of the PR for that. ## 📝 Summary of Changes New flag `--xla_gpu_command_buffer_keep_collectives_out_of_outputs` (default false). head_commit.message:
PR #52604: [XLA:GPU] Refresh the B300 target spec from a live B300

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52604

#ai-generated

Fixes #52602

### Status quo
`b300.txtpb` (from #34116, source device not stated) has 158 SMs, a 1.965 GHz clock, 297021865984 B of memory, 7.936 TB/s and a 135528448 B L2. A live B300 SXM6 AC reports 148, 2.032 GHz, 287416123392 B, 7.672 TB/s and 132644864 B. The spec also has no `name`, so `SpecMatchesLiveDevice` skips on B300, and it lacks the fields that the refreshed b200/gb300 specs carry.

### Why
Deviceless/AOT compiles for `GpuModel.B300` should see the same device as an on-device compile. With the current spec, for example, a bf16 elementwise kernel gets 128-bit vectors deviceless and 256-bit on device (65536 vs 32768 blocks for 2^26 elements).

### Design
- Regenerated from the `gpu_target_config.pbtxt` that `--xla_dump_to` writes on a B300 (jaxlib 0.12.1.dev20261108).
- Dropped the per-host fields `numa_node`, `pci_bus_id`, `kernel_mode_driver_version` and the top-level `runtime_version`. Of the checked-in specs, only vr_nvl72.txtpb has them.
- Kept `driver_version: "13.0.0"`, as in gb200/gb300/h100_sxm. `SupportsMovedChildCommands` reads it, so leaving it unset would turn moved child commands off for deviceless compiles.
- Kept `device_description_str: "NVIDIA B300"`, since `gpu_topology.cc` maps "NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC" to it.
- `name` is the live `NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC`.
- Version fields follow b200.txtpb: runtime/toolkit 13.2.0, cuDNN 9.23.0, CUB 3.1.2. The live machine had pip CUDA 13.5 and cuDNN 9.28.1, which describe the test environment rather than the device.
- Data only, no code change. #52432 adds memory bus width to other specs and does not touch this file; whichever lands second can add it here.

### Tests
- A deviceless JAX compile against the new spec gives the same `loop_add_fusion` launch (32768 x 128) as the live B300 does; the old spec gives 65536 x 128.
- The spec parses: deviceless compiles with it succeed.
- If the current values describe another B300 SKU, this should become a separate spec rather than a replacement (question in #52602).
- Not run: `CudnnDevicePropsTest.SpecMatchesLiveDevice` on B300 (needs a `--config=cuda` build). Only one B300 SKU (SXM6 AC) was available, so other B300 SKUs may report different values.

Copybara import of the project:

The checked-in b300.txtpb has no device name and does not match a live B300 SXM6 AC: it has 158 SMs instead of 148, a 1.965 GHz clock instead of 2.032 GHz, 297021865984 bytes of memory instead of 287416123392, and 7.936 TB/s and a 135528448-byte L2 instead of 7.672 TB/s and 132644864 bytes. It also lacks the fields the other refreshed Blackwell specs carry. Regenerate it from the gpu_target_config dumped on a B300, keeping device_description_str and using the same runtime/toolkit/cuDNN/CUB version convention as b200.txtpb.

SupportsMovedChildCommands in command_buffer_conversion_pass.cc takes the

display_title: PR #51750: Fix a use-after-free race in AcquireClique

head_commit.message:
PR #51750: Fix a use-after-free race in AcquireClique

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51750

📝 Summary of Changes

In AcquireClique, the rendezvous callback looks up a cached clique under state.mu, where it returns a raw LockableGpuClique* and called Acquire() after releasing the mutex. the only thing keeping the clique alive is its entry in state.cliques. Then a concurrent run on the same clique key could take state.mu, decide the clique's parent isn't a superset of its split_from, take safety_lock, erase the entry and destroy the clique. The first run would then call Acquire() on freed memory, a use-after-free.

🎯 Justification

A potential use-after-free crash

🚀 Kind of Contribution

Please remove what does not apply: 🐛 Bug Fix
Copybara import of the project:

--
3a60d7d124c4e12d07573bcadd6b2e83e5c4913e by TJ Xu <tjx@nvidia.com>:

returns a shared_ptr from AcquireClique that keeps the clique alive until Acquire() returns

--
13135fd2ec24decd11e38cba3e92afbdf1eef863 by TJ Xu <tjx@nvidia.com>:

put the owner and the lock in the same struct to keep their lifetimes the same

Merging this change closes #51750

head_commit.message:
PR #52604: [XLA:GPU] Refresh the B300 target spec from a live B300

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52604

#ai-generated

Fixes #52602

### Status quo
`b300.txtpb` (from #34116, source device not stated) has 158 SMs, a 1.965 GHz clock, 297021865984 B of memory, 7.936 TB/s and a 135528448 B L2. A live B300 SXM6 AC reports 148, 2.032 GHz, 287416123392 B, 7.672 TB/s and 132644864 B. The spec also has no `name`, so `SpecMatchesLiveDevice` skips on B300, and it lacks the fields that the refreshed b200/gb300 specs carry.

### Why
Deviceless/AOT compiles for `GpuModel.B300` should see the same device as an on-device compile. With the current spec, for example, a bf16 elementwise kernel gets 128-bit vectors deviceless and 256-bit on device (65536 vs 32768 blocks for 2^26 elements).

### Design
- Regenerated from the `gpu_target_config.pbtxt` that `--xla_dump_to` writes on a B300 (jaxlib 0.12.1.dev20261108).
- Dropped the per-host fields `numa_node`, `pci_bus_id`, `kernel_mode_driver_version` and the top-level `runtime_version`. Of the checked-in specs, only vr_nvl72.txtpb has them.
- Kept `driver_version: "13.0.0"`, as in gb200/gb300/h100_sxm. `SupportsMovedChildCommands` reads it, so leaving it unset would turn moved child commands off for deviceless compiles.
- Kept `device_description_str: "NVIDIA B300"`, since `gpu_topology.cc` maps "NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC" to it.
- `name` is the live `NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC`.
- Version fields follow b200.txtpb: runtime/toolkit 13.2.0, cuDNN 9.23.0, CUB 3.1.2. The live machine had pip CUDA 13.5 and cuDNN 9.28.1, which describe the test environment rather than the device.
- Data only, no code change. #52432 adds memory bus width to other specs and does not touch this file; whichever lands second can add it here.

### Tests
- A deviceless JAX compile against the new spec gives the same `loop_add_fusion` launch (32768 x 128) as the live B300 does; the old spec gives 65536 x 128.
- The spec parses: deviceless compiles with it succeed.
- If the current values describe another B300 SKU, this should become a separate spec rather than a replacement (question in #52602).
- Not run: `CudnnDevicePropsTest.SpecMatchesLiveDevice` on B300 (needs a `--config=cuda` build). Only one B300 SKU (SXM6 AC) was available, so other B300 SKUs may report different values.

display_title: PR #52201: [XLA:GPU][Triton] Fix collective while-loop command buffer tests on ROCm

head_commit.message:
PR #52201: [XLA:GPU][Triton] Fix collective while-loop command buffer tests on ROCm

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52201

📝 Summary of Changes
On ROCm, where HIP graphs have no conditional nodes: CommandBufferConversionPass drops the WHILE command and captures the loop body into a command buffer nested inside the WhileThunk. The 20-collective while-loop tests for all-gather, all-reduce and all-to-all additionally asserted that the kWhile thunk itself is captured, which only holds on CUDA, so those two expectations are now guarded by Capability().IsCuda().

`CountThunksInDump` only tracked command buffer membership for top-level thunks, so thunks inside a nested kCommandBuffer were counted as being outside one. Track the indentation of the innermost enclosing kCommandBuffer instead.

🎯 Justification
On ROCm, the `Twenty*InWhileLoopWithCudaGraphs` multi-gpu single host triton collective op tests (`all_gather_e2e_test`, `all_reduce_e2e_test`, `all_to_all_e2e_test`) fail because HIP graphs have no conditional nodes.
These tests must therefore be adapted so that they pass on both Cuda and ROCm.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
Please remove what does not apply: 🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Support CTA cluster synchronization in bitonic sort

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Support CTA cluster synchronization in bitonic sort

Previously, the MLIR bitonic sort emitter only fused compare-and-swap steps
within one CTA's shared-memory tile (`tile_size`), requiring a separate global
kernel launch per step once `xor_mask >= tile_size`.

On Hopper+ GPUs (`sm_90+`), extend tiled bitonic sort across 2-CTA clusters
using distributed shared memory (DSMEM) and cluster barriers, doubling the
in-kernel sort span and cutting global round-trips:
- Propagate optional `se::ClusterDim` through `LaunchDimensions` and custom
  kernel specs to set driver cluster dims and `"nvvm.cluster_dim"` on kernels.
- Add `gpu::BarrierScope` (default `Workgroup`) to `xla_gpu.sync_threads`,
  forward it to `gpu.barrier` in `LowerTensors`, and lower cluster barriers to
  aligned `nvvm.cluster.arrive` and `nvvm.cluster.wait` in `LowerToLLVMGPU`.
- Support `"xla_gpu.dsmem"` on shared-memory accesses in `LowerTensors` by
  mapping the base pointer to the peer CTA's shared memory via `nvvm.mapa`.
- Emit 2-CTA clustered bitonic sort kernels when stages exceed `tile_size`,
  unclustered blocks exceed SM count, and cluster padding is at most 12.5%
  (capping at 2 CTAs avoids GPC fragmentation and register pressure). Cross-CTA
  steps use `gpu.cluster_block_id x` and DSMEM; full tiles keep the unrolled
  fast path while bounds-checked and post-cluster `kIntraTileSort` merges stay
  rolled.

head_commit.message:
PR #52104: [ROCm] [CUDA] Keep recorded collectives out of output allocations under VA remapping Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52104 Shared GPU code (CUDA and ROCm). This is mainly beneficial to ROCm, where re-recording a collective on every execution is costly. from CUDA side change is not regressive but not greatly beneficial either (Tested on B300). from ROCm side I'm trying find ways to reduce the recapture whenever possible this is one of the PR for that. ## 📝 Summary of Changes New flag `--xla_gpu_command_buffer_keep_collectives_out_of_outputs` (default false). With it, `COLLECTIVES` in command buffers and `SKIP_TEMP` / `SKIP_PROFILED`, values that a collective which may be recorded defines or reads stay out of output allocations (`BufferAssigner::Options::must_not_live_out`). Host send/recv are not matched. GPU buffer assigner options are now built in `CreateBufferAssignerOptions`. ## 🎯 Justification ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Collective recorded in a command buffer
COLLECTIVES + SKIP_TEMP / SKIP_PROFILED + flag"] --> B{"Where is its operand / result?"} B -- "Before: output allocation (buffer reuse)" --> C["New address every execution"] --> D["Collective re-recorded
on every initialization"] B -- "After: temp allocation" --> E["Stable address"] --> F["Collective skipped
at initialization"] classDef bad fill:#fde2e2,stroke:#c0392b,color:#1a1a1a classDef good fill:#e2f5e6,stroke:#27ae60,color:#1a1a1a class D bad class F good ``` Trade-off: values that shared an output allocation now need temp space. Buffer assignment runs before the command buffer conversion pass, so the predicate also covers collectives that end up outside a command buffer (for example below `xla_gpu_graph_min_graph_size`). Off by default; `ALWAYS_UPDATE` (default) is unchanged. ## 🚀 Kind of Contribution ⚡️ Performance Improvement ## 🧪 Unit Tests - `gpu_memory_space_assignment_test`: 7 new tests (when the predicate is installed, including flag off; result and async collective-group placement, with a flag-off control; collectives filter; which instructions and positions match; host send/recv not matched; live-out result). - `gpu_compiler_test`: `CollectiveCommandBuffersKeepCollectivesOutOfOutputs` (`maybe_live_out` of the all-reduce's allocation under `ALWAYS_UPDATE`, and under `SKIP_TEMP` with the flag off and on). ## 🧪 Execution Tests `collective_ops_command_buffer_test` on MI355X: `SKIP_TEMP` and `SKIP_PROFILED` with the flag on give the same results as `ALWAYS_UPDATE`. The two `RaggedAllToAll` peer-access cases fail in every mode on this ROCm build (`InitializeCrossDeviceBarrier is not implemented`), independent of this change. B300 was tested on the previous revision, where the predicate was on whenever these modes were set. Copybara import of the project: -- 26a0f2d1645ca4fe1f1b8c2c78267ac00333cb81 by magaonka : [ROCm] Keep recorded collectives out of output allocations under VA remapping - With COLLECTIVES in command buffers and SKIP_TEMP / SKIP_PROFILED, a collective whose buffer shares an output allocation is re-recorded on every execution. - Set must_not_live_out on GPU so those buffers stay in the temp allocation. - Build the GPU BufferAssigner options in CreateBufferAssignerOptions. - IsCommandBufferCollective maps opcodes through GetCollectiveOpType. -- 841452b0ed4617e51d1dfd0f561cd31fbecb0165 by magaonka : [ROCm] Gate collectives out of output allocations behind a flag - Add xla_gpu_command_buffer_keep_collectives_out_of_outputs (default false). CreateMustNotLiveOut installs the predicate only when it is set. - Do not match host send/recv: they lower to host send/recv thunks, which are never recorded. - gpu_compiler_test checks maybe_live_out of the all-reduce's allocation instead of comparing temp allocation sizes. Merging this change closes #52104 FUTURE_COPYBARA_INTEGRATE_REVIEW=https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52104 from ROCm:fix/collectives-out-of-output-allocations-upstream 841452b0ed4617e51d1dfd0f561cd31fbecb0165 PiperOrigin-RevId: 1020839779

display_title: PR #51750: Fix a use-after-free race in AcquireClique

head_commit.message:
PR #51750: Fix a use-after-free race in AcquireClique

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51750

📝 Summary of Changes

In AcquireClique, the rendezvous callback looks up a cached clique under state.mu, where it returns a raw LockableGpuClique* and called Acquire() after releasing the mutex. the only thing keeping the clique alive is its entry in state.cliques. Then a concurrent run on the same clique key could take state.mu, decide the clique's parent isn't a superset of its split_from, take safety_lock, erase the entry and destroy the clique. The first run would then call Acquire() on freed memory, a use-after-free.

🎯 Justification

A potential use-after-free crash

🚀 Kind of Contribution

Please remove what does not apply: 🐛 Bug Fix
Copybara import of the project:

returns a shared_ptr from AcquireClique that keeps the clique alive until Acquire() returns

put the owner and the lock in the same struct to keep their lifetimes the same

display_title: PR #52443: [XLA:GPU] Add support probe and dense fallback for cuDNN ragged-dot fusion

head_commit.message:
PR #52443: [XLA:GPU] Add support probe and dense fallback for cuDNN ragged-dot fusion

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52443

📝 Summary of Changes

Make the cuDNN ragged-dot fusion fall back to the regular dense expansion when
cuDNN cannot build a plan for a given ragged dot. The fusion stays behind
`xla_gpu_experimental_use_ragged_dot_fusion`, whose default is unchanged.

- `RaggedDotRewriter` takes an optional `is_supported_by_cudnn_fusion` callback.
  A ragged dot that passes the existing static gates (cuDNN version, Ampere+,
  binary libraries enabled, unbatched 2D lhs / 2D-3D rhs / 1D group sizes,
  F16/BF16 types, single ragged dim) is only left for the fusion rewriter if
  the callback also returns true; otherwise it is expanded to dense dot as before.
  The decision has to be made here because `RaggedDotRewriter` runs before layout
  assignment, while `RaggedDotFusionRewriter` runs post-layout, where a dense
  expansion would produce layout-less ops.
- New `IsRaggedDotSupportedByCuDnn` (`ragged_dot_cudnn_support.{h,cc}`, CUDA-only):
  builds a scratch module with the ragged dot, runs `RaggedDotFusionRewriter`,
  and asks cuDNN about the resulting fusion via `ResolveCudnnSupport` +
  `GetAvailablePlanCount(...) > 0`, for both JIT and deviceless compilation
  (honoring `xla_gpu_cudnn_deviceless_compilation_mode`). Only a positive answer
  counts as supported; no plans and errors all fall back to dense, with the
  reason logged at `VLOG(3)`.
- Plumbing: virtual `GpuCompiler::IsRaggedDotSupportedByCuDnn` (default
  `Decision::Forbid`, overridden in `NVPTXCompiler`). `RunOptimizationPasses` now
  receives the `StreamExecutor*` and derives `is_deviceless` from it.

🎯 Justification

With `xla_gpu_experimental_use_ragged_dot_fusion` enabled, a ragged dot that
passes the static gates but that cuDNN has no engine for (e.g. mixed
token/weight dtypes) fails compilation hard in the cuDNN fusion compiler. With
this change such a ragged dot compiles via the dense path instead, so the flag
can be turned on safely later.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

N/A.

🧪 Unit Tests:

- `RaggedDotRewriterTest.CudnnSupportCallbackDecidesFusionOrExpansion`: with the
  fusion enabled, a callback returning true leaves the ragged dot in place; a
  callback returning false expands it to dense.
- `RaggedDotRewriterTest.ExpandsWhenBinaryLibrariesDisabled`.
- `ragged_dot_cudnn_support_test`: supported and unsupported ragged dots.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Use named barrier 1 for single-block phase transitions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Use named barrier 1 for single-block phase transitions.

This prevents `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION` errors when generalizing MultiStageFusion to column reduction and transpose that emit block barriers themselves.

In `ThreadBlockSpecializedFusion`, consecutive single-block phases synchronize via `bar.sync 0` across all `max_threads` of block 0, while partial-CTA sub-kernels (`sub_threads < max_threads`) rewrite intra-phase barriers to `barrier.sync 0, sub_threads` on the same hardware barrier 0. When a partial-CTA reduction or transpose runs as a single-block phase followed by another single-block phase, threads with `tid >= sub_threads` skip the sub-kernel and reach the trailing `bar.sync 0`, arming barrier 0 with thread count `max_threads` while active threads arrive at barrier 0 with thread count `sub_threads`, raising `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION`.

name: CI
display_title: Retry buffer assignment with direct operand reuse only

head_commit.message:
Retry buffer assignment with direct operand reuse only

The heap simulator lets a temporary reuse the buffer of an operand that it only reads through other positions (e.g. a `bitcast` or a `get-tuple-element`). This lowers the peak memory, but the reused buffer has to stay at the same offset for longer, which makes it harder to pack. For some modules the fragmentation therefore grows by more than the peak memory shrinks.

So this change makes the fallback in `BufferAssigner` try all its strategies a second time without this kind of reuse (`HeapSimulator::Options::may_reuse_operand_buffers_through_other_positions`) if none of them fits the memory limit. As before, each color keeps the assignment with the lowest memory usage. This way a module that is close to its memory limit does not need more memory than it would without the reuse through other positions.

Nothing changes for modules where one of the existing strategies fits. For the others, the fallback now runs twice as many heap simulations.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1020813629

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Validate dimensions and overflow in `xla::ifrt::Shape::NumElements`

`xla::ifrt::Shape::num_elements()` multiplied dimension sizes without checking for negative dimensions or `int64_t` overflow, allowing shapes constructed outside `Shape::FromProto` to wrap `int64_t` modulo 2^64 or return negative or canceled-sign element counts.

Add `Shape::NumElements()` returning `absl::StatusOr<int64_t>` when any dimension is negative or the element count overflows `int64_t` (reused by `Shape::FromProto` and `ifrt_proxy`'s `ArrayMemRegion::FromZerothElementPointer`), and update `Shape::num_elements()` to `CHECK_OK` on `NumElements()` while keeping `Shape(absl::Span<const int64_t>)` zero-overhead at construction time.

Existing `Shape` tests only checked overflow in `Shape::FromProto` and small non-negative dimensions in `Shape::num_elements()`.

display_title: [IFRT] Add absl_nonnull to RCReference aliases and API pointer arguments

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Add absl_nonnull to RCReference aliases and API pointer arguments

IFRT reference-counted handle aliases (`ArrayRef`, `BundleRef`, `ValueRef`, and `DeviceListRef`) and core IFRT API pointer arguments (such as `Device*` and `LoadOptions` in `Client`, `Client*` in deserialization helpers and `IfrtIrProgramCompiler`, and `SerDes` in `RegisterSerDes`) are required by contract to be non-null, yet lacked compile-time nullability annotations.

Mark `RCReferenceWrapper` with `ABSL_NULLABILITY_COMPATIBLE` (with matching nullability-annotated RTTI overloads in `rtti.h`), add `absl_nonnull` to `ArrayRef`, `BundleRef`, `ValueRef`, `DeviceListRef`, and non-null pointer arguments across IFRT interfaces, and mark `DeserializeExecutableOptions` in `Compiler::DeserializeLoadedExecutable` `absl_nullable`.

display_title: PR #52875: [XLA:CPU] Prevent unsafe buffer reuse in oneDNN fusions

head_commit.message:
PR #52875: [XLA:CPU] Prevent unsafe buffer reuse in oneDNN fusions

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52875

A fused FP32 matmul followed by `maximum(product, zeros)` can return negative values on the oneDNN/ACL path. XLA permits the output to reuse the zero operand's buffer, but matmul overwrites those zeros before maximum reads them. The regression returns `[[6, -6], [-12, 12]]` without the fix instead of `[[6, 0], [0, 12]]`.

Use a shared CPU alias policy during copy insertion, scheduling, buffer assignment and AOT loading. Custom fusions deny inferred input/output reuse by default; YNNPACK retains the usual HLO shape/use checks. oneDNN's compiled partition requirements are unavailable during compilation. Fusion remains enabled, with potentially higher buffer memory use and protective copies for aliased inputs. Saved executable formats and existing allocations are unchanged.

Validation:

- 39 focused test executions pass across AArch64 QEMU N1, SVE256 and SVE512: allocation rules, internal and aliased zero inputs, YNNPACK reuse, and AOT export/load.
- Removing only the copy-insertion policy makes both new aliased-input regressions fail while the original internal-broadcast regression still passes.
- The original 17x23 by 23x19 reproducer passes six numerical comparisons across those profiles, still using `gemm:acl` with the fused maximum.
- Clang-format 17.0.6, buildifier 6.4.0 and whitespace checks pass.

A previous broader sweep found an unrelated SVE512 batched-matmul mismatch using oneDNN's `brg:sve_512`. It predates this change and remains unresolved. These are correctness tests under emulation, not native performance measurements.

[XLA:CPU] Prevent unsafe buffer reuse in oneDNN fusions

Keep oneDNN fusion outputs separate from their inputs because the
compiled partition's in-place requirements are unavailable during
buffer assignment. This prevents fused matmul from overwriting the
zero operand before maximum applies ReLU.

Add allocation and execution regressions while preserving buffer reuse
for ordinary loop fusions.

Deny inferred buffer reuse for custom fusions unless their runtime
supports it. Preserve YNNPACK's existing HLO sharing rules and share
CpuAliasInfo between compilation and AOT loading.

Cover aliased oneDNN inputs through copy insertion and execution, plus
YNNPACK reuse. Keep the regression enabled on AArch64.

Signed-off-by: Pablo Marquez Tello <pablo.tello@arm.com>

Merging this change closes #52875

display_title: Limit non-direct operand reuse to bitcast and get-tuple-element

head_commit.message:
Limit non-direct operand reuse to bitcast and get-tuple-element

Allowing `HeapSimulator::RunComputation` to reuse operand buffers through arbitrary forwarding positions also matches asynchronous completion instructions such as `copy-done` and `collective-permute-done`, whose buffers are defined at the corresponding `-start` instruction. Reusing those short-lived transfer buffers for long-lived consumers welds them into a single colocation group across the combined lifetime, which can increase heap fragmentation in `GlobalDecreasingSizeBestFitHeap`.

So this change restricts non-direct operand buffer reuse in `HeapSimulator::RunComputation` to `bitcast` and `get-tuple-element` operands.

CDNA wavefronts are 64 wide, so a concat boundary at 32, 96, 160, … split a wavefront but escaped the penalty.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add margin-aware early stopping to autotuner profiling.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add margin-aware early stopping to autotuner profiling.

***Problem:*** GPU autotuning runs multiple timed passes and L2 cache flushes unconditionally on every candidate, wasting compilation time on clearly slower or long-running kernels while a fixed duration cutoff misranks close medium-duration contenders due to first-run post-synchronization clock transients.

***Solution:*** Add competitive margin-aware early stopping in `GpuProfiler::Profile` (configurable via `ProfileOptions::adaptive_early_stopping`) that stops after the first timed run when transient timing error is negligible or a candidate falls outside the statistical contender margin of the fastest candidate seen on the same `GpuInputBuffers`, while preserving multi-run averaging for close contenders.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1015915803

display_title: [TF/XLA] Finalize Bazel 8 Bzlmod cleanup and mark XLA extensions reproducible.

head_commit.message:
[TF/XLA] Finalize Bazel 8 Bzlmod cleanup and mark XLA extensions reproducible.

Following the Bazel 8.8.2 and Bzlmod default switch, a few build regressions and
transitional workarounds remained across TensorFlow and XLA: Windows `.pyd`
imports in the 251-259 character path range failed with
`ERROR_FILENAME_EXCED_RANGE`, `bazel mod show_repo --all_repos` could not
resolve `envoy_api` cleanly, `custom_op_cc_header_only_library` dropped
external include paths without `-external_include_paths`, and 12 deterministic
XLA module extensions were not marked reproducible.

* Pin `envoy_api` to `0.0.0-20260130-84e8436` in TensorFlow's `MODULE.bazel`
  (matching XLA) so `bazel mod show_repo --all_repos` resolves cleanly.
* Fix Windows `ERROR_FILENAME_EXCED_RANGE` when loading `.pyd` extensions in the
  251-259 char path range under Bzlmod (`rules_python`'s
  `_WindowsExtensionPathFinder` only added `\\?\` at `>= 260` chars, missing
  Win32 `LoadLibraryExW` `.manifest` probing) via
  `//third_party/py:rules_python_windows_long_path.patch`.
* Remove obsolete `--features=-external_include_paths` and
  `--host_features=-external_include_paths` from `.bazelrc` and XLA's
  `tensorflow.bazelrc` (now that `rules_cc` is `0.2.25 >= 0.2.22`), propagate
  `CompilationContext.external_includes` through `system_includes` in
  `xla/tsl/transitive_dependencies.bzl` (`_transitive_parameters_library_impl`,
  used by `custom_op_cc_header_only_library` such as
  `//tensorflow/core:framework_headers_lib`), and remove the duplicate
  `common:windows --features=compiler_param_file`.
* Mark all 12 remaining deterministic XLA module extensions reproducible via
  `mctx.extension_metadata(reproducible = True)` under `third_party/` and
  `build_tools/pjrt_wheels/`.
* Replace deprecated `$(location ...)` with `$(execpath ...)` in
  `tensorflow/tools/pip_package/BUILD`, bump `BAZEL_VERSION` to `8.8.2` in
  `tensorflow/tools/ci_build/install/install_bazel_from_source.sh`, and
  document the Bazel 8.8.2 / Bzlmod and C++/CUDA dependency upgrades in
  `RELEASE.md`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1020428804

name: CI
display_title: Clear incompatible tiled sharding on TopK custom calls in xla::TopkRewriter.

head_commit.message:
Clear incompatible tiled sharding on TopK custom calls in xla::TopkRewriter.

`CreateTopKCustomCall` creates the 2D `TopK` custom call, its
`get-tuple-element` outputs, and its input/output `reshape` and `transpose`
instructions via `sort->AddInstruction(...)`, which calls
`SetupDerivedInstruction` and copies `sort`'s sharding whenever the tuple tree
structure matches (`ShapeUtil::CompatibleKind`). When `sort` has rank > 2 (so
its input is reshaped to 2D before `TopK` and reshaped back afterward) or is 2D
with `sort_dim == 0` (so its input is transposed before `TopK` and transposed
back afterward), a tiled sharding on `sort` has the wrong rank or transposed
tile dimensions for the 2D `TopK` custom call, its `get-tuple-element`
instructions, and (for 1-operand sorts) the input/output `reshape` and
`transpose` instructions. Clear tiled sharding on `sort` before creating those
instructions while preserving non-tiled shardings (such as `{manual}` or
`{replicated}`) and 1D/2D `sort_dim == 1` tiled shardings.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1020684245

name: CI
display_title: Separate `dfs_hlo_visitor_with_default.h` from `//xla/hlo/ir:hlo` into a standalone header-only `//xla/hlo/ir:dfs_hlo_visitor_with_default` target.

head_commit.message:
Separate `dfs_hlo_visitor_with_default.h` from `//xla/hlo/ir:hlo` into a standalone header-only `//xla/hlo/ir:dfs_hlo_visitor_with_default` target.

`dfs_hlo_visitor_with_default.h` is a consumer header layered on top of `:hlo` (`DfsHloVisitor`, `HloInstruction`, `HloComputation`, `HloModule`); nothing in `:hlo` includes it. Update `:dfs_hlo_visitor_test` and downstream targets that directly include `dfs_hlo_visitor_with_default.h` to depend on `//xla/hlo/ir:dfs_hlo_visitor_with_default`.

name: CI
display_title: Avoid dereferencing end() in HloSharding::GetSubSharding.

head_commit.message:
Avoid dereferencing end() in HloSharding::GetSubSharding.

`HloSharding::GetSubSharding` constructed a subspan of `tuple_elements_` by
taking `&*begin_it` and `&*(begin_it + leaf_count)`. When the sub-tuple extends
to the end of `tuple_elements_` or is an empty tuple, this dereferences
`tuple_elements_.end()`, which is undefined behavior and traps under libc++
bounded iterators.

Slice `absl::MakeConstSpan(tuple_elements_).subspan(sharding_index, leaf_count)`
instead, after checking `sharding_index + leaf_count <= tuple_elements_.size()`.
